articles.text: Set up a new BidoCMS installation The first-time setup wizard creates a limited database identity and the first administrator for an installation. Use the secure address provided by the server operator. An existing installation shows an already-configured state and links to sign-in. Before starting - Confirm the site address with the server operator. The wizard records the public site origin from the setup request. - Ask the operator to prepare the deployment's private MongoDB connection and application secrets. The wizard uses the MongoDB configuration supplied by the deployment. - Have an administrator email address and a place to store the administrator and database passwords securely. These accounts serve different purposes. Database 1. Open the installation's Set up BidoCMS screen, usually at the site address followed by /setup. 2. Enter the Database name for this site and a Database user dedicated to the installation. The database name is normalized to lowercase. The database account gets access to its own database. 3. Enter a Database password of at least 16 characters, or use Generate. Preserve it in the appropriate password manager or deployment records. 4. Choose Test database. Wait for the status to confirm the database test. 5. Test again after any change to the database fields. A successful test of the current configuration is required before installation. First administrator 1. Enter the Administrator login email. This account receives full BidoCMS access. 2. Enter an Administrator password of 12 to 72 UTF-8 bytes with a letter and a number, or use Generate. 3. Choose Install BidoCMS. Keep the page open while deployment and installation progress are displayed. The application may restart once. 4. When the page says Your BidoCMS site is ready, choose Open BidoCMS and sign in using the administrator email and password. 5. Configure your site details, review installed pages and theme, set up mail delivery, then add roles and team accounts as needed. Resolve setup problems | What you see | What to check | | --- | --- | | The setup screen says BidoCMS is already configured | Use the sign-in link. Ask the operator to confirm the host if this was supposed to be a new deployment. | | The form highlights Database fields or has no successful test | Correct those fields and test again. Ask the operator to verify the deployment MongoDB connection if valid values continue to fail. | | The form highlights the login email or password | Correct the highlighted fields first. Use the generated password option if needed. | | Setup could not be loaded | Use the retry action. If the condition persists, ask the operator to check the HTTPS site address and deployment readiness. | | Installation appears paused during a restart | Keep the setup page open during the reconnect step and wait for the completion or error message. Record the displayed error before contacting the operator. | Provide the operator with the site address, the affected setup step, and the error text. Keep passwords and database connection strings out of support messages. See also Sign in and recover access, Settings General, and Site General settings.

Find your way around the BidoCMS panel The BidoCMS panel is the administration workspace for one installation. Open the sign-in address supplied by your administrator. Each installation can have its own site domain and CMS address. Open a workspace 1. Sign in with your administrator-provided email. Complete a verification code or password-change prompt if the panel asks for one. 2. Choose a workspace in the sidebar. On a narrow screen, use the Open navigation button to open the menu drawer, choose a workspace, and return to the panel. 3. Open any tabs inside the workspace. A feature may show additional tabs after you select a page, image, role, or account. 4. Use the browser's Back and Forward buttons to move through the panel areas you visited. Some workspaces support a direct browser link to a selected item. Opening that link still requires permission to access the item and its workspace. Use the header | Control | Purpose | | --- | --- | | Open Website | Opens the public website. Check the public page there after publishing. | | Publish All Pages | Starts a site-wide publication for roles allowed to publish. Use it for changes intended to affect the whole site. | | Contextual actions | The current workspace can add controls such as Refresh notifications, a page publication action, or a theme-related publication action. | | Help | Opens the English documentation for BidoCMS in another browser tab. | On mobile, the Website and publishing actions button opens a compact menu for site and publishing actions. The side menu and the header actions serve different purposes. The product name and version appear in the header. A site can also show its own name and image. Which menus you can see The sidebar and workspace tabs are filtered using your role. For example, access to Users → Roles and Users → Users can differ. An administrator role is also required for several operational settings, even where their menu is visible to a delegated account. Access to a menu can also depend on whether a parent menu is included in the same role. Select your display name in the sidebar to open Profile. Use Log out to end your browser session, especially on a shared device. | If you are trying to… | Start here | | --- | --- | | Change public content or upload images | Pages, Images, or Site, depending on the change | | Confirm a change is publicly visible | Publish, then Open Website | | Find site health and recent activity | Notification, Monitor, or Console | | Manage team access | Users → Roles or Users → Users | | Change panel defaults or configure connections | Settings | | Reuse website content in another CMS | Export | | Handle products, orders, customer portals, or another site-specific workflow | Check the installed site's theme or app for its own documentation. The shared BidoCMS menu catalog does not define a universal commerce or customer-management workspace. | If a colleague can see a control that is missing from your screen, tell your administrator the full menu and tab name, the action you were trying to take, and which installation you signed into. On a phone, first check the open navigation drawer and the tab strip. See also Sign in and recover access, Manage roles, and Publish site changes.

Update your profile and secure your account Select the displayed account name in the sidebar to open Profile. All authenticated users can use Profile even when the Users administration menu is hidden from their role. Profile details 1. Open Profile details. 2. Edit the fields you want to update. 3. Select Save profile and look for Profile saved. The display name in the sidebar updates after a successful save. | Field | Purpose | | --- | --- | | First name, Middle name, Last name | Personal name fields stored on your account. | | Display name | Name shown in the sidebar. The sidebar falls back to first and last name if the display name is empty. | | Phone number | Optional contact number on the account. | | X username | Optional X profile username. Changing it updates your account details. | | Email | Read-only from Profile. Ask a CMS administrator to change the email used for sign-in. | Change password 1. Open Security → Change password. 2. Enter your Current password, then your New password and Repeat new password. 3. Use at least eight characters with a letter and a number and keep the password within 72 UTF-8 bytes. 4. Select Change password. Sign in again after the panel redirects you to the login screen. Turn on two-step authentication 1. Open Security → Two-step authentication. 2. Enter your current password and select Set up two-step authentication. 3. Scan the QR code with your authenticator app. 4. Enter the six-digit Verification code and select Verify and enable. 5. Confirm the panel shows Enabled. At future sign-ins, enter the current code for this account when asked. While the panel displays Awaiting verification · not enabled yet, the QR code has been created and enrollment is pending. If the setup expires, choose Cancel setup, start again, and scan the new code. Canceling before verification leaves the account's existing setting unchanged. Keep the QR and six-digit codes private. Turn off two-step authentication Open Security → Two-step authentication, enter your current password, and select Disable two-step authentication. Verify that the status changes to Not enabled. See also Sign in and recover access.

Sign in, sign out, and recover access Use your installation's login page with the email associated with your BidoCMS account. Each installation has its own access and administrator. Sign in 1. Open the login address given to you by your administrator. The common entry point is /login on the installation's site. 2. Enter your Email and Password. 3. Optionally choose Remember me for 30 days on a trusted device. Without it, the site uses a browser-session cookie and an eight-hour authentication token. 4. Select Log In. 5. If two-step authentication is enabled, enter the current six-digit Authenticator code and select Confirm. 6. If prompted to change a temporary password, complete that step before opening the panel. When finished, open the sidebar and choose Log out. On a phone, open the navigation drawer first. Replace a temporary password An administrator may send or privately share a temporary password when creating or resetting an account. Use that password to sign in, including the current authenticator code if prompted. Enter New Password and Repeat New Password, then select Save and Continue. The new password must differ from the temporary one, contain at least eight characters including an ASCII letter and digit, and use at most 72 UTF-8 bytes. The first-password challenge expires after ten minutes. If it expires, return to sign-in and repeat the process with the temporary password. The panel opens once the new password has been accepted. Recover a forgotten password 1. Select Forgot Password on the login form when the link is available. 2. Enter your account email and select Send Reset Link. 3. Check the inbox and spam folder. Open the current reset link from the email. 4. Enter and repeat a strong new password, select Reset Password, and sign in with the new password. Recovery requires a configured, enabled mail transport. Reset links expire and are single-use. A successful reset ends existing sessions. If a reset link is invalid, expired, or already used, request a new link. If Forgot Password is absent, ask the site's administrator to reset your password. Troubleshoot login | Symptom | What to check | | --- | --- | | Correct-looking credentials fail | Confirm the site address and email first. An administrator can verify whether the account is active and belongs to this installation. | | A verification code is rejected | Use the current code for this installation in your authenticator app. Try again after the next code appears if the current code was near expiration. | | You no longer have access to your authenticator | Contact the site administrator to confirm identity and review account recovery. Keep recovery and authenticator codes private. | | You can sign in but a menu is missing | Ask your administrator to check the specific menu and submenu grants. | | The login screen mentions reviewing website access | Complete sign-in to review the website's access request. Approve it only if the site and request match your intended action. | See also Profile and security and Manage user accounts.

Check recent website activity in Google Analytics live The Google Analytics live card in the Notification workspace reads realtime traffic for the Google Analytics 4 property connected to this BidoCMS installation. This dashboard card is available to the built-in administrator with the appropriate workspace access. Read the card | Value | Meaning | | --- | --- | | Active users · 30 min | Google Analytics active users in its most recent thirty-minute window. | | Active users · 5 min | Active users in its latest five-minute window. | | Top pages by views | Recent pages ordered by views when the property returns those rows. | | Active users by country | Available geography rows for recent active users. | | Active users by device | Available device category rows for recent active users. | | Updated | The time the displayed data was retrieved. | The panel refreshes this card about every minute while Notifications is open and the browser tab is visible. Use Refresh notifications for an immediate dashboard refresh. A counter can show zero when the property records no activity in that window. An em dash indicates an unavailable value. If the card does not show the expected data 1. Open Settings → Analytics and verify the connected Google property. 2. Check that the public website sends GA4 data to that property. Open the live site from an eligible test browser and allow time for the realtime view to refresh. 3. If the card shows a connection prompt, review the Google account's property permissions and reconnect where required. 4. If supported breakdowns remain blank, verify what the property exposes in GA4 Realtime. For historical traffic, open the page-level Analytics workspaces. See also Connect Google Analytics, Page-level Google Analytics, and Use Notifications.

Use and rearrange the Notifications dashboard Notification is the sidebar entry for the Notifications dashboard for site status, integrations, and operations. It loads each available card independently so you can use results as soon as they arrive. Open and refresh the dashboard 1. Choose Notification in the sidebar. If your role can access it, your installation can open here by default. 2. Allow the placeholders in the visible cards to resolve. One card can finish while another is still loading. 3. For a new snapshot, use Refresh notifications in the header area. On mobile, open Website and publishing actions if the control is tucked away. 4. Open the relevant workspace when a card offers a shortcut such as Backups, Open console, or Open Settings. | Card | What it shows | | --- | --- | | Google Search performance | Whole-site clicks and impressions over the last 30 days. | | Pages Google hasn’t indexed | Eligible published pages with a confirmed inspection issue, plus coverage of pages without a confirmed status. | | Site pages | Page-type counts for total, published, and Google-indexed versions. | | Google Analytics live | Active users and recent traffic breakdowns for the connected GA4 property. | | Latest backup | The latest completed backup recorded by the installation, along with the parts included. | | CPU & RAM usage | Six-hour history for CPU and RAM, with missing spans and operational markers when available. | | Server console | The latest 50 captured log lines. | Rearrange cards Drag the move handle in a card header and drop it at the intended position. With a keyboard, focus the move handle and use the arrow keys to move the card, or Home and End to move to the beginning or end. Your browser stores the order for your account on that installation. Other browsers, profiles, or devices may start with the default order. Why a card may be missing or empty Most cards are shown only for cms admin. CPU & RAM usage can appear if the role has Monitor access, but the underlying system API still requires the built-in administrator. If that card cannot load for a delegated role, ask the site administrator to check resource usage. A disconnected integration can show a connection prompt. A connected source can still lack recent measurements or inspection results. If one card says it could not load its data, use Refresh notifications and check that card's connection or source workspace if it persists. See also Search and site pages cards, Google Analytics live card, and System health cards.

Read Google Search and site-page cards Open Notification in the sidebar for three related views of search activity and published content. Index coverage and clicks come from Search Console. BidoCMS provides its own page totals and publication counts. Google Search performance The chart reports Clicks and Impressions for the whole connected site over the last 30 days. Each metric has its own chart scale. Hover a day to see its values, or focus the chart and use the arrow keys. Dashed lines mark preliminary data. If coverage is still being collected, the card shows how many days are included in the displayed totals. A blank or unavailable value means there was no usable measurement. Pages Google hasn’t indexed The list shows published pages marked for indexing whose available inspection results report that they are not indexed. Each reported entry can include the URL, coverage state, and date checked. 1. Find the page and read the recorded coverage state. 2. Choose Inspect to open Search Console. If a page-specific inspection link is unavailable, copy the displayed URL into the Search Console inspection tool. 3. Review the coverage details in Google. Correct the underlying issue in BidoCMS, publish the change, and use Google's Request indexing option when appropriate. The dashboard shows a separate count of pages without a confirmed status. All checked pages are indexed refers to pages with results. If the card reports no eligible pages, check whether the intended URL is published and marked for indexing. Site pages Read Total, Published, and Indexed by page type or in the totals row. Each language version counts separately. The indexed column can show an unknown value when Search Console is disconnected or indexing coverage is unavailable. If only some pages have confirmed results, the card can show how many published pages were checked. Use the page's own Search Engines tab for page-specific inspection history. If the dashboard asks you to connect Google, open Settings → Search Console and confirm the correct property. See also Connect Search Console and Use Notifications.

Check backups, server load, and logs in Notifications The operational cards in the Notification workspace provide an at-a-glance view of backup history, six-hour resource use, and recent server logs. Availability depends on the installation and your account's permissions. Latest backup Check for Completed, the date and time, and whether Database, Files, or both were included. The card uses the latest recorded completed backup with an archive. An uploaded or newly discovered file does not substitute for a completed run in this card. Select Backups to open the dedicated workspace and review its records. If the card says No completed backup yet, check whether a backup configuration exists and has run. When a scheduled backup was expected, check its automatic status and storage destination. CPU & RAM usage The chart summarizes CPU and RAM percentages from the application's runtime scope over the last six hours. Inspect chart points with your pointer or keyboard. Missing measurements appear as gaps. Where recorded, the chart can mark process restarts, server restarts, and factory resets. Open Monitor for longer ranges, additional metrics, and alert rules. Server console The server console card shows the last 50 lines from the captured application log. Scroll within the card or select Open console to view more lines, refresh, or download the captured buffer. Look for the timestamp of the backup, publication, or configuration action you are investigating. Share only the relevant log lines after reviewing them for credentials or identifying data. See also Configure backups, Monitor server resources, and Read the server console.

Site logo, favicon, and web app manifest Open Site → General to change the CMS site branding and configure the installable web app. The BidoCMS product badge and the site's own branding both appear in the CMS header when site branding is available. Set the site logo or favicon 1. Import the image into Images, if it is not already in the album. 2. Open Site → General. 3. Under Site logo or Favicon, select Choose from album. 4. Select one image and confirm the picker selection. The field shows a preview. 5. Select Save at the bottom of the page. Use default clears the selected image for that field after you save. The logo and favicon are separate selections. Choosing an image requires access to the Images album. If the file disappeared or BidoCMS cannot prepare it, select another image from the album. Configure the web app manifest The Web app manifest (JSON) field accepts a JSON object. Leave the field blank to use the built-in manifest with the domain name and site logo. To change the app's presentation, enter only the fields you want to override, then save. { "name": "Example Studio", "short_name": "Example", "theme_color": "#17324d", "background_color": "#ffffff" } Select View active manifest to open /manifest.json in a new browser tab. Check the active values there after saving. The form rejects invalid JSON and top-level arrays. Property names and string values need double quotes, and object properties cannot end with a trailing comma. Verify a branding change Reopen the CMS and check the site name and logo in the header. Open the public site to check the favicon displayed by the browser. Check the active manifest after a logo, domain, or manifest change. A browser may keep the previous favicon visible until its cache updates. Site settings · Upload images

Sitemap, robots.txt, and AI discovery files Use Site → General to manage publicly served discovery files. Make sure Site Address reflects the live site before rebuilding or checking any of these files. Sitemap Address Enter a relative path such as hidden-sitemap/sitemap.xml in Sitemap Address. Select Save, then select Update sitemap to request a rebuild without publishing every page. Open in new tab beside the field opens the address configured in the form. The generated index links to sitemap content grouped by page type. Review Pages → Main Content for each page that should appear. A page must meet the publisher's publish and index conditions and have a valid URL and eligible page type. Recheck the sitemap after updating the page, rebuilding as needed. Robots File Edit Robots File and save to update /robots.txt. Keep the final contents public and check for unexpectedly broad disallow rules. The field's Open in new tab action opens the public file for inspection. Page-level index controls the generated page's robots metadata. Robots File provides site-wide crawling directives. Inspect both when diagnosing whether a URL can be crawled or is marked for indexing. LLMs File and LLMs Full File Use LLMs File for a short Markdown overview of the site and important public URLs. Use LLMs Full File when you want a longer public guide. Save, then open /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt using the buttons beside the fields to verify the output. Keep confidential and administrative material out of these files. Website context for AI is a separate field for BidoCMS image-description generation. If the output does not match the form Check that the form was saved and the public domain opens correctly. Use Update sitemap for an outdated sitemap. When the site uses S3 and a CDN, review Publish settings and verify from the public domain after deployment completes. Site settings · Page main content · Page indexing and inspection

Site settings Open Site → General for installation-wide settings such as the public address, branding, discovery files, and code inserted into generated pages. Use a language tab in Site for the title, description, and theme of one language. General fields | Field | What it controls | | --- | --- | | X Account | The site's X account value used by publishing metadata. | | Site Address | The public website address. Use an absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL such as https://example.com. The panel uses it for Open Website and preview links. Sitemap and public-page URLs also depend on this value. | | Site logo | Image next to the site name in the CMS and the source for installed app icons. | | Favicon | Image shown in the browser tab. | | Website context for AI | Website description, audience, brand voice, and relevant services for AI-generated image descriptions. The limit is 8,000 characters. | | Sitemap Address | Relative path to the sitemap index. The default generated path is hidden-sitemap/sitemap.xml. | | Web app manifest (JSON) | Optional settings for the installable web app. View active manifest opens the resolved manifest. | | Robots File | Contents of the public robots.txt file. | | LLMs File | Contents of the public llms.txt file, typically a short Markdown guide to the website. | | LLMs Full File | Contents of the public llms-full.txt file, typically an extended Markdown guide. | | short link domain | Public base address for copied page short links. The panel uses Site Address when this field is blank. | | Header Start | Markup inserted at the start of the generated HTML head. | | Header End (CSS) | CSS added near the end of the head inside a style element. | | Body Start (JS) | Script and supported noscript content inserted near the start of the page body. | | Body End (JS) | Script and supported noscript content inserted near the end of the page body. | Change and verify a setting 1. Open Site → General and edit the relevant field. 2. Select Save at the bottom. Wait for the confirmation. 3. Use Open Website or the file's Open in new tab action to check the public result. Check the publish queue for changes that affect generated pages. The address fields accept HTTP or HTTPS URLs without credentials, query parameters, or a fragment. Enter the site address without a trailing slash. Keep access keys, private URLs, and internal notes out of the discovery files and generated code fields because their contents can reach the public site. Choose the smallest scope for code changes Use Site → General for site-wide code, Site → Site NodeType for pages of one type, and Pages → Extra for one page language. During generation, BidoCMS combines these three scopes in that order. Branding and the web app manifest · Sitemap and discovery files · Page-level code · Publishing

Site image tag list Open Site → Image Tags to maintain the list of tag names available in the image album. Tags can support categories such as Team, Products, and Office. Work in the panel 1. Open Site → Image Tags. 2. Edit image tags list data, keeping one name per line. 3. Select Save to update the list. 4. Open Images, select an image, and open Details → Tags to assign one of the listed tags. The Site editor operates on the complete active list. Names omitted from the submitted list are deactivated. Adding the same name again reactivates the tag. Review the other names before saving a change. Assign tags to individual images in Images. Tag folders in the album show images already associated with a tag and are separate from regular upload folders.

Website languages and theme variables Website languages control which language versions you can edit for public pages. Open Site and select the language tab to edit one version, or select + to add a language. The panel language and direction are configured separately in Settings. Add a website language 1. Open Site → +. 2. Choose Language. The form proposes a Website sub address based on the language code. 3. Check Website sub address. Use the public path prefix for that language, such as /fr. 4. Enter the language-level Title and Description. 5. Select the Theme for this language. 6. Review and fill in any theme variables that appear. 7. Select Save. 8. Open Site page types and review the template mapping for the new language. 9. Open Pages, select an existing page, and check its new language tab. A site can have one configuration entry per language. Saving a new language adds a draft detail to existing pages tied to the site's page types. These details start with a generated placeholder URL and with index and publish off. Edit the localized content and URL before enabling either option. Edit the existing language Open the site's language tab and update Website sub address, Title, Description, Theme, or the variables supplied by that theme. Language is fixed on each existing entry. Theme variables are fields defined by the selected theme. Their names and use differ across themes. If you switch themes, check the visible variable fields and recheck the page type mappings. The CMS attempts to match the site page type to a template with the same name in the selected theme. A missing match needs manual attention. Delete a language Open the specific language tab, select Delete, then confirm. Removing a language deletes its page details and related content for pages associated with the site's types, including text, FAQs, videos, specifications, and comments. It also removes that language's template mappings and language-specific theme variable values. The CMS prevents deletion of the final language. Page types and template mappings · Page main content · Publishing

Site page types and theme template mappings Open Site → Site NodeType to manage site page types. A site page type is the option selected under Pages → General → Node type. It connects the same page to a theme template for each configured website language. Add and map a page type 1. Open Site → Site NodeType and select Add Site Type. A new editable row appears. 2. In Type name, enter a descriptive name such as Article or Service. 3. In color, enter a color value such as #475569. This color marks pages of the type in the page tree. 4. For each selector named with a theme and language, choose the matching template for that language. 5. If this page type needs extra code, enter it in the four scope-specific fields. 6. Select Save on the row. 7. Open a page's General tab, choose the type in Node type, and save. Preview the result in each active language. The available templates come from the theme assigned to that language. When a language's theme changes, review its mappings under Site NodeType. If a template needs changes, use the theme editor or import an updated theme. Type-level header and body fields | Field | Output | | --- | --- | | Header Start | Markup inserted toward the beginning of the HTML head. | | Header End (CSS) | CSS added to the head. | | Body Start (JS) | Script or supported noscript content near the start of the body. | | Body End (JS) | Script or supported noscript content near the end of the body. | BidoCMS combines site-wide, type-level, then page-language content in each slot. Changes to a shared type can affect multiple pages on publishing. Delete an unused type Use the row's delete icon and confirm. If the CMS reports that pages still use the type, open those pages under Pages → General, assign another suitable type, and save before trying again. Keep a language-to-template mapping for every type you intend to publish. Website languages · Page General tab · Theme schema assignments

Publish settings, S3, and CDN Open Publish → Settings to choose where generated files are published and configure the CDN. Generated files are always written to the server. Enabling Publish on S3 also uploads them to object storage and requires the Cloudflare CDN option. Configure S3 publishing | Field | What it sets | | --- | --- | | Publish on S3 | Enables object storage in addition to local output. The panel enables CDN automatically in this mode. | | Region | Storage provider's region. | | Bucket | Destination bucket name. | | Endpoint URL (optional) | Custom endpoint for an S3-compatible provider when needed. | | Destination Path (optional) | Key prefix inside the bucket. | | Access Key (set only) | Storage access key. The panel displays whether one is configured. | | Secret Key (set only) | Storage secret key. The panel displays whether one is configured. | | Storage Sync Cron (optional) | Schedule for copying local storage to S3. For example, 0 3 * * * requests a daily run at 03:00 in the deployment's scheduling timezone. | Leave a set-only credential field blank to retain its current stored value. Enter a new value only when configuring or replacing that credential. Configure Cloudflare and save 1. Confirm the live hostname under Site → General → Site Address. 2. Enable CDN if using Cloudflare with local publishing. S3 publishing requires it. 3. Check CDN Provider. The current panel supports Cloudflare. 4. Supply the Cloudflare API Token if it is not configured. 5. Select Save Settings. BidoCMS looks up the Cloudflare zone from the saved site's hostname and can update the CDN and DNS configuration. 6. Review the detected zone name and ID. If saving fails, check that the site address has the intended hostname, the zone is available to the token, and the bucket and both storage credentials are configured when S3 is enabled. Resolve any cron validation error before saving. Test or sync the saved configuration Select Test Configuration after saving. The result shows pass, fail, or skipped checks with explanatory details. Depending on enabled settings, it tests the S3 connection, Cloudflare token and zone, domain-to-zone match, and whether the domain serves content from S3. Correct failed settings and test again. Use Sync Now to start a storage-to-S3 sync against saved settings. The last sync result shows the trigger, time, counts of checked and uploaded files, and errors. Sync copies applicable locally generated files. Use a publish action when the site needs to regenerate content. Site Address · Publish Queue

Preview and publish pages BidoCMS saves content in the panel and generates website output through publishing. After saving a page, use the preview and publish controls in the header, or open Publish → Publish Queue to watch the background queue. Preview one page 1. Open Pages and select the page in the tree. 2. Save each edited tab or text block. 3. Select preview of page on a single-language site or preview selected node on a multilingual site. 4. Confirm Publish Test and wait for the generated preview to open in a new tab. 5. Check the affected languages, links, images, mobile layout, and any page-specific changes. These actions require publish queue access. A preview is temporary. If no browser tab opens after confirmation, check whether the browser blocked pop-ups or the page lacks a valid template or URL. Publish one page or the whole site - To publish one page, select it in Pages, choose publish page or publish selected node, and confirm Publish Node. The action queues the page and may also queue directly dependent pages, such as pages that display its content. - To queue every page, select Publish All Pages in the CMS header and confirm Publish Site. - To open the public website, select Open Website. The target comes from Site → General → Site Address. - On small screens, open the header actions menu to access website and publication actions. Normal generation uses each language version's publish setting and the configured template mappings. Test generation can show a language version with publish off. Always check the public language and address afterward. Changing publish to off or saving a new URL stops future generation at the previous path. Existing generated files can continue to be served. If a previously public path must disappear or redirect, ask the administrator to verify local output, remote storage, and the CDN for that specific path. Read the Publish Queue Open Publish → Publish Queue. The progress area shows the number of remaining pages and progress for the currently observed batch. Select Details to see individual entries and whether they started. Select Hide Details to return to the progress summary. The panel updates the queue while the tab stays open. Idle — queue is empty means the currently visible queue has drained. Verify the public page afterward. If a page stays outdated, check its language's publish flag and template mapping. When serving from a CDN, also check the publish configuration and the public result after cache updates. Page main content · Publish configuration · Theme activity

Redirects Open Redirects to tell the public site where to send requests for an old path. Published redirect rules send an HTTP 301 response. Use this when moving a public page or sending an obsolete path to a replacement. Add an internal redirect 1. Select Add Redirect Rule. 2. In Old URL, enter the original public path, such as /old-services. 3. In New URL, enter the replacement path, such as /services. 4. Select Save and wait for Redirect rule saved. 5. Open the old URL and verify it reaches the intended destination. Use the exact old path. A path on the same website can be entered with its leading slash. A page's Pages → Main Content → Redirect URL also lets you set an internal destination for that page's current address. Point an old path to another domain 1. Add or edit a rule in Redirects. 2. Enter the full destination, including https:// or http://. 3. Select Save. Review the displayed address in Confirm external redirect. 4. Enter your Current password and select Confirm and save. External destinations require access to the Redirects menu and password confirmation when saving. Use the Redirects workspace for this operation. If a change to a page's URL keeps an existing external redirect, update the associated rule through Redirects. Edit, remove, or troubleshoot a rule Edit the two fields on the applicable row and save. To remove a rule, choose its trash icon and confirm. Check for duplicate source paths, the correct public language prefix, and the intended destination. Use a fresh browser session to verify a recently changed rule because browsers can cache 301 responses. On the CMS origin, an existing public HTML file can be served before a stored redirect is checked. If the old page still loads, check for generated output at that path as well as CDN caching. Page URLs and canonical URLs · Website languages

Page comments Open Pages, select a page and language, then select Comment when it is available. This tab requests comments for that page language. Current release behavior The Comment panel currently fails to render existing comment records correctly. It also has no working panel controls for approving, replying to, or deleting comments. An empty or broken tab cannot establish whether the public page has comments. Ask the site administrator which comment workflow the active theme supports. If this tab is missing, check the account's Pages → Comments menu permission. The site's public comment workflow also depends on the theme. Page tree and language selection

Page-specific code in Extra Open Pages, select a page and language, then choose Extra. Changes apply to the selected language version of this page. Use the following fields when a page needs markup, CSS, or script beyond what its theme already provides. | Field | Generated page location | | --- | --- | | Header Start | Markup near the beginning of the HTML head. | | Header End (CSS) | CSS wrapped in a style element near the end of the head. | | Body Start (JS) | Script or supported noscript content near the beginning of the body. | | Body End (JS) | Script or supported noscript content near the end of the body. | Save, preview, and remove code 1. Insert only the markup or code needed for the page. The CSS field takes CSS, with the style wrapper applied by BidoCMS. 2. Select Save. 3. Use Test Publish for the selected page and check every affected language. 4. Verify the expected behavior before publishing the page. 5. To remove the customization, clear the field, save, and publish again. Code from Site → General, Site → Site NodeType, and Pages → Extra is combined in that order for each slot. If the same behavior appears twice, inspect all three scopes and the template. Use Site → General to intentionally apply code across the whole site and Site → Site NodeType to apply it for a single type. Site settings · Site page types · Preview and publish

Add and reorder page FAQs Open Pages, select a page language, then choose FAQ. Questions and answers belong to the selected language. Display on the public page depends on its theme template. Add a question and answer 1. Select Add Question. 2. Enter the Question and Answer in the new row. 3. Select the row's Save. 4. Repeat for other entries. Open a collapsed row by selecting its question title. 5. Save any edits before leaving the tab or switching language. An entry is complete when both fields contain nonblank text. The core automatically manages the FAQPage reference using complete entries in their saved order. The page schema preview shows the generated entry when applicable. When there are no complete entries, the automatic reference is removed. Check Page Schema to understand whether the structured data appears. Reorder or remove questions Drag the row's handle to the new position, or focus the handle and use the up and down arrow keys. The panel saves the new order and announces the result. If order saving fails or the list changed in another session, reopen it before sorting again. To remove a question, use Delete FAQ on the row and confirm. Check the preview after editing and publish to update the live page.

Page General tab Open Pages, select a page, and open General. These settings apply to the page entry shared across all its language versions. | Field | How it is used | | --- | --- | | Shenase | Internal name displayed in the page tree. Choose a name that makes the page easy to find. | | Node type | The site page type, which selects the available theme page template for each language. The type can also affect the available text fields and structured content. | | Parent | Read-only view of the page's actual parent in the tree. Use the tree's move operation to change it. | | Virtual Parent | Additional references to other pages selected in a multi-select field. Themes can include virtual children in listings or related-page groups. | Rename a page or change its type 1. Open the page's General tab. 2. Edit Shenase, select Node type, or update Virtual Parent. 3. Select Save. 4. For a type change, review the Text, Specification, and Schema tabs before publishing. The new template can use a different collection of fields. 5. Preview the page in each affected language. Use Main Content → Name to change the public breadcrumb label for one language. Use Main Content → URL for the public path. Shenase only changes the panel's internal tree label. Troubleshoot a missing template or field Open Site → Site NodeType and confirm that the selected page type maps to a template for the current language. If a text block is missing, confirm that the selected template defines the corresponding section. A recent theme or type change may require reopening the page to refresh the available fields. Tree and hierarchy · Site page types · Page public content

Add supplies, tools, and steps to a page Open Pages, select a page and language, then choose How To. This workspace records the supplies, tools, and steps for a procedure separately from the page's rich-text sections. Use the How To tab | Button | Fields to complete | | --- | --- | | Add Supply | supply value, such as a material used up during the task. | | Add Tool | Tool value, such as a reusable item used to carry it out. | | Add Step | title for the action and body for its instructions. | 1. Select the appropriate add button. 2. Fill in the fields of the new row. 3. Select Save on that row. 4. Repeat as needed. Each supply, tool, or step is saved separately. 5. To remove an item, select its trash icon and confirm. In a multilingual site, repeat the process for each public language that needs the instructions. Check that the theme template displays the fields on the public page. Use a preview before publishing. Page text editor · Site page types

Page Main Content and SEO settings Open Pages, select a page and its website language, then choose Main Content. This tab holds the public address, primary metadata, image selection, and publishing options for that language. | Field | What to enter or check | | --- | --- | | Name | Public short name used in the breadcrumb list. | | URL | Relative public path such as /admissions. Use a unique path. The form converts spaces to hyphens when saving. | | Short link | Read-only compact address assigned to this language version. Select Copy to copy the full URL instead of only the displayed path. | | canonical URL | Optional preferred URL for canonical metadata. Leave blank to use the computed address. A relative path uses the site's base address and language prefix. A full canonical URL can be supplied when intentional. | | Redirect URL | Optional internal destination path for requests to this page's address. Use the Redirects menu for new or changed external destinations. | | Title | Browser tab title and generated HTML title. Enter a clear localized title. | | Description | Generated meta description for this language. | | H1 | Primary visible heading when the theme displays the page H1. | | index | Generated page robots metadata. Off produces noindex and nofollow. | | publish | Whether this language version is included in normal public page generation. | | Select Image | Opens the image album to choose up to three page images. Save Main Content to commit the selection. The theme determines how it displays the images. | Edit or translate a page 1. Select the page in the tree. 2. On a multilingual site, open the exact website language you want to change. 3. Enter the localized Name, URL, Title, Description, and H1. 4. Check whether a canonical override or redirect is needed. Review the index and publish checkboxes. 5. Select images if the page needs them and choose Save. 6. Update the separate Text tab for rich-text blocks. Save each block individually. 7. Preview and publish. Site language settings contribute the language root used by generated canonical and alternate links. The core publisher writes the stored URL path to the output. Verify the live path, canonical URL, alternate language links, and sitemap agree, especially when the installation also uses a language prefix. Changing Title and H1 can have different effects because the theme renders headings and the CMS generates metadata. Troubleshoot a URL or short link - Selected URL is not free means another page detail already uses the path. Enter a distinct path. - The Short link control needs an assigned detail number and a nonempty page URL. Copy uses short link domain from Site → General, with Site Address as fallback. A clipboard error may require granting clipboard access in the browser. - Changing the public URL requires reviewing links that use the old path. Create a redirect if the old address should lead to a replacement. - If a saved page is missing from the public site, check publish, the language's template mapping, and the Publish Queue. Indexing and inspection · Page schema

Page Schema and JSON-LD preview Open Pages, select a page and language, then select Schema. This tab shows the structured data references and optional manual JSON-LD for that page version. Review or override page type defaults The hint above Schemas for this node shows the page type and whether the page is using its defaults or a custom list. Use the selector and Add to assign a schema. Select × on an assignable chip to remove it. After saving a custom list, manage these references on the page rather than relying on later type-level assignment changes. A chip marked Auto is managed by the publisher. The page selector excludes the automatic FAQ reference. For FAQ structured data, complete questions and answers in the selected language can create an automatic reference. Edit the FAQ entries to change its source content. Add manual JSON-LD Use Manual schema (appended to generated output) for an additional JSON object or an array of objects. Enter JSON-LD body data directly in the field. Use valid JSON with double-quoted property names and no trailing commas. This field is separate from the schema format templates in Schema → Definitions. Preview, save, and publish 1. Select Refresh in Generated schema preview to ask BidoCMS to build a preview using the displayed choices and manual value. 2. Read the generated JSON-LD or the manual-schema parse error. Review the values and URLs against your public content. 3. Select Save to keep the page's references and manual schema. 4. Preview and publish the page. Verify the generated output for the same language. If the preview is empty, check the page type mapping, assigned definitions, and source data for that language. A saved preview is useful for comparing the panel's generated data with the public result after the publishing queue drains. Schema definitions · Default schema by page type · Preview and publish

Page specifications Open Pages, select a page language, and open Specification. Specifications are named data fields that the selected page type or theme can use to display attributes on the website. Fill in existing specification values 1. Locate the field under its family group. 2. Enter a value or select an option. A field with multiple slots accepts more than one value up to its configured maximum. 3. If the field has a description area, add the optional descriptive text. 4. Select the row's Save. Repeat for other fields. The panel can show corresponding values from other languages for reference. Saving applies to the current language detail. The theme controls which attributes appear publicly and how they are labeled. Create a specification definition Select Add New Specification. The first site node type selector actually chooses the value's data type. The second chooses the site page type. | Field | Purpose | | --- | --- | | name | Name or key of the specification. | | family | Group heading used to organize fields. | | description | Guidance shown alongside the value input. | | maximum select data | Number of value slots in the editor. | | title | Optional label shown alongside the name. | | need extra text | Adds a separate description input for the value. | | First site node type field | Data type. Choose String, Number, Float, Boolean, or List. | | list data | For List, enter each allowed option on its own line. | | Second site node type field | The intended site page type for the specification. | Save the definition. Reopen the tab to load any new available value row. A definition's Save configures the field. The value row's Save stores the content for the page. Use the definition card's trash icon and confirmation to delete a custom definition after reviewing where it is used. If the field is missing, check the selected language, the page's Node type, and the specification's target type. Page General tab · Site page types

Find, create, and move pages Open Pages in the CMS sidebar. The page tree shows the shared structure of the website. Each entry is called a page or node. Its tree name, type, and parent are shared across languages. A page's website content is edited separately for each language. Open an existing page 1. Open Pages. 2. Use the arrow beside a page in the tree to expand its children. 3. Select the page name to load its tabs. 4. On a multilingual installation, select an existing language tab to view that language's content. Use the outer General tab for fields shared by all languages. 5. On a small screen, use Browse pages to reopen the tree and Hide page list to give the editor more room. The selected page, language, and supported tab are reflected in the panel URL. You can bookmark or share the panel link with a teammate on the same installation who has the necessary access. The sidebar label, tree language, and website language can differ. The tree displays a search node name field in this release. If typing does not return results, expand the applicable tree branches or reopen a saved page link. The current panel does not connect that field to the search handler. Create a page under an existing page 1. Expand the tree to the intended parent. 2. Select the plus icon on that parent. 3. Confirm Add New Node. 4. In General, change Shenase from its generated value and choose Node type. 5. In Main Content, give the page a real public URL and complete its public metadata. Check publish and index explicitly for each language. 6. Fill in each theme-defined Text section and the relevant structured tabs. 7. Preview the page and publish it using the header actions. The new page is created immediately when you confirm. The new-page action creates language details with placeholder names and URLs and with publish and index enabled. Check these values before anyone queues a site-wide publish. The separate Site → + language workflow creates new language details for existing pages with both options off. An empty tree can display Add First Node. If that action does not select the new root automatically, reopen Pages and select the entry from the refreshed tree. Move a page in the tree On desktop, drag the page row to a different page's row to place it at the end of that parent's children. A drop marker between rows can place the page after a closed item or first inside an open item. Expand both branches afterward to verify the resulting parent and order. Open General to check the read-only Parent. Moving the tree entry changes the hierarchy. To change its public path, update URL in each affected language and review existing links and redirects. The tree workspace has creation and move controls, with no page deletion action. Use the page's publish setting to stop future normal generation. If a page was already public, ask the administrator to verify and remove obsolete generated output where necessary. Page settings · Page language and SEO fields · Preview and publish

Add video details to a page Open Pages, select the page and language, then choose Video. Video rows hold the URLs and duration used by a theme's video section. Work in the panel 1. Select Add Video. 2. In embed URL, enter the provider's embed address when the theme uses an embedded player. 3. In content URL, enter the video content address appropriate to the theme. 4. In Duration (seconds), enter the positive whole-number duration. For a two-minute video, use 120. 5. Select Save on the video row. 6. Preview the result on the page to verify the theme displays it and the player works. Use the row's delete icon and confirm to remove it. Save or delete the correct language's entry. If the panel reports an incorrect duration, enter a value greater than zero. If a video is saved but missing in the preview, check the URLs and whether that page template uses the video section. Page tree · Preview and publish

Page text and rich-text editor Open Pages, select a page and language, then open Text. The selected theme template defines the available sections. A layout might contain one main field, multiple named blocks, or no editable rich-text section. Open and save a text section 1. Find the section you want in Text and select Edit text. 2. Make changes in the rich-text editor. The editor can create an empty section when you first open it. 3. Use the toolbar's save icon or Save & close from the editor menu. Wait for the save confirmation. 4. Reopen the section to verify the stored content as needed, then preview the public page. The editor has a separate close control. Use the save action to persist edits before switching tabs or closing. The template controls the number and names of text fields, supported formats, and image variants available to a section. Edit metadata such as Title and H1 under Main Content. Formatting, media, and links The toolbar includes undo and redo, formatting, heading and block styles, alignment, indents, numbered and bulleted lists, colors, links, media, symbols, text direction, and HTML source. Selecting text can show shortcuts for bold, italic, link, headings, quote, lists, and AI writing when available. Use Insert/edit image to select an image from the album. The section's template configuration determines which image sizes the picker can provide. Where available, use the selected link's Add nofollow action to set its rel value. Use the HTML/source action only when your task requires it, and preview formatting on the public page after changes. Text insights | Section | What it shows | | --- | --- | | Document outline | Heading levels and heading text. Select a heading to navigate to it. | | Search Console queries | Web search queries for the saved page URL when Search Console is connected and you have access. The editor uses up to the last 90 days and orders results by impressions. | | Word & phrase frequency | Frequent single words and phrases. Phrase-length filters, hover highlights, and match navigation help review repeated text. Common words are excluded for the text language. | | Document overview | Counts for words, unique words, characters, and headings. | | AI writing assistant | AI writing controls for selected text or the current document, subject to provider configuration and access. | Drag the separator to adjust the available width where the layout shows the insights panel beside the editor. With the separator focused, the arrow keys also resize it. Home and End set its smallest and largest available widths. Review AI suggestions and save the text after applying changes. If Search Console queries are unavailable, first save a valid page URL for the selected language and check the page's Search Console connection and data. AI writing assistant · Site page type mappings · Media album · Publishing

Generate and edit images with AI Use Images → Generate image to create an image in the current regular folder. To work from an existing original, select an image and open Details → Source. Generate a new image 1. Open a regular image album folder and select Generate image. 2. Choose an enabled provider key and model. 3. Enter Your prompt. Add reference images if applicable. 4. Depending on the selected model, review Aspect ratio, Quality, and the other available options. Fields can include Action, Constraints, and Image name. 5. Review Final prompt when displayed, then select Generate image. 6. Wait for the job to finish. The image is saved in the current folder and opened in the album. Edit an existing image 1. Open the image's Source tab and choose an enabled provider key. 2. Select Freehand outline, Point-by-point outline, or Rectangle to guide the main edit area. Release to finish a freehand shape. For point-by-point, finish with Enter or a double-click. Use Undo selection or Clear selections to correct the guide. With the canvas focused, Escape cancels the current outline and Delete or Backspace removes a point or the latest guide. 3. Enable Edit without an area guide to use the prompt alone. 4. Select Edit with AI, describe the desired change, then choose Generate edited image. 5. Review the new image stored in the original folder. The selected regions guide the edit. The model can adjust the rest of the image as well. An edited result is a new album image. Use image size variants when the goal is cropping, scale, rotation, or a specific output size. If the form reports a missing AI connection, check the enabled API key and model in AI & Agent. If a selection is too large to send, use a smaller original image or use the whole-image option when suitable. Image album · Image descriptions

Image album, uploads, and folders Open Images to organize the reusable media album. Regular folders hold image files. Virtual tag folders show files associated with a tag. Open a folder and select images - Click a thumbnail to select one image. Hold Shift while clicking to add images when the picker allows multiple selections. - Double-click a folder to open it. The .. folder returns to its parent. - Select one image and choose Details, or double-click it, to open its detail tabs. - When opening the album from a page or another picker, choose the permitted number of files and click Select. Save the originating page's field when required. When available, the panel URL reflects the open folder, tag, image, and image detail tab. A saved panel link remains subject to the recipient's access. Import or organize files 1. Open a regular folder. 2. Select Import and choose one or more image files. The uploader accepts up to 5 MB per file. 3. Wait for the upload messages. A single successful upload can open its detail panel automatically. 4. Select New Folder to create a subfolder, if needed. The initial name is new folder. 5. Edit the label of a regular folder or image by selecting its displayed name when the inline name input is available. The album also accepts an image dragged onto the gallery. Use Import for several files at once. An image's title can be initialized from its EXIF description or filename. Caption and alt text can come from EXIF values. Open Detail and review the imported metadata, especially for meaningful images. Delete an item or troubleshoot an import Select the folder or images, choose Delete, and confirm the requested deletion. Deleting a regular folder also deletes its child folders and the images in it. The root folder cannot be deleted. Check where images are used in pages or as site branding before removing them. If Import or New Folder reports a virtual directory restriction, navigate to a regular folder. For a failed file upload, check the file size and use a supported raster format such as JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, AVIF, or TIFF. The album accepts an image per upload request and can send multiple files from Import. If the gallery lists no matching items in a tag folder, check the image's tag assignment. Alternative text, titles, captions, and tags · Crop and rotate image sizes · AI source image

Image alt text, titles, captions, and tags Open Images, select an image, and choose Details. Use Detail for localized text and Tags for organizing the album. Edit the metadata of one language 1. Open the Detail tab. 2. Find the part of the form with the intended website language. 3. Enter Alternative text, Title, and Caption as needed. 4. Select the Save beside that language. 5. Repeat for the other configured languages. Alternative text describes the meaningful content of the image. Title gives the image a label. Caption provides supporting context if the template shows it. Use the actual language of each form section. The theme determines which metadata it includes in the public page. Write descriptions with AI 1. Select Write descriptions with AI. 2. Choose a configured provider key and model. 3. Review the list of website languages and edit Instructions as needed. Use Reset to standard prompt to restore the default wording. 4. Enable Include website context to send the context from Site → General → Website context for AI, if configured. 5. Select Generate and save for all languages. 6. Review the saved fields in every language, then manually correct any wording as needed. This action replaces alternative text, title, and caption across all configured website languages and saves the generated values automatically. If the action asks for setup, enable AI and a provider key first. Assign or remove an image tag Open the Tags tab and choose Add New Image Tag. Select an Image Tag from the list and click Save. Use the row's delete action to remove the assignment. The tag itself can still be available for other images. If Tags is absent, check your role and whether the site has any image tags. Theme code editor Open Themes → Code editor, or open a thumbnail in Themes → Themes to load a specific theme into the workspace. The editor contains a file tree and tabs for open source files. Open, edit, and save a file 1. Expand the relevant directories in the file tree. 2. Select the file to open it in the editor. 3. Make the intended change. An asterisk on a tab signals unsaved edits. 4. Use Ctrl+S or Command+S while focused in the editor, or Save file where displayed. 5. Wait for the result and reopen the file if you need to confirm the stored content. A tab's × closes it. Save relevant tabs before opening another theme or creating a theme, because those actions can replace the workspace. The editor supports language-aware editing for formats including HTML, CSS, JavaScript, JSON, and Markdown. File tree actions Open a file or folder's ⋯ menu or its context menu. Available actions depend on the selected item and your access. | Item | Actions | | --- | --- | | File | Open, Edit file name, Delete file. | | Folder | Expand, Edit folder name, Delete folder, Add folder, Add file, Add component. | | Recognized component | Preview from its tree row or Show from its context menu, where offered. | When adding a component, choose its intended name. BidoCMS recognizes a component directory when it contains a same-name HTML file, such as ExampleCard/ExampleCard.html. Styles and JavaScript can use matching peer files. When the component uses translated language keys, keep its language.json aligned with the languages it supports. Check dependencies and references before renaming or deleting files. Preview and apply Open Component preview to inspect the component using the Mobile, Tablet, and Desktop controls. Select Refresh to reload it after saving. Theme gallery · Figma workflows · Publishing

Build theme components from Figma Open Themes → Code editor → Connect Figma if your role includes Themes → Code editor → Figma. This tool uses a selected Figma layer and AI model to generate workspace component files. Check the connection The installation needs a server-configured Figma access token with access to the file, and an enabled AI credential and model. Browsing team projects also needs a Figma team ID and applicable team access. A direct file link can be used when the team browser is unavailable. Choose a file and a layer 1. Open the theme workspace you intend to edit. 2. Select Connect Figma. 3. Paste a Figma file URL or key in Open by file link and choose Open file, or browse Team projects if configured. 4. Open the intended page. Drill into frames and nested layers as needed. 5. Choose Select on the intended frame or layer. Verify the selected name and type under Selection. Use the breadcrumb or Back to change levels. If the project list is empty but the file is accessible, use the direct file link. If the connection is forbidden, ask the administrator to check the configured token and file sharing. Build and review the output 1. Choose the AI credential and model in the dialog. 2. Select Build component for a reusable component, or Build page section for a larger page section. 3. Wait for generation and the Generated and saved message. BidoCMS writes the returned components into the open theme workspace. 4. Open each generated file in the code editor. Check layout, accessibility, styles, interactions, and theme placeholders with component and page previews before publishing. Theme code editor · AI provider settings

Browse, create, and import themes Open Themes → Themes to browse registered themes, import a packaged theme, or create a new workspace. A theme provides page templates, components, assets, languages, and optional variables used to generate public pages. Browse the gallery Your themes lists the available theme entries and their preview images. Select a theme thumbnail to open that theme in the code editor if your role has access. The theme selected for each public language is configured in Site languages. Create an empty theme 1. Select Create theme and confirm that a new workspace can be opened. Save unsaved work in the existing workspace first. 2. Enter Theme name and Author / producer. Short description is optional. 3. Select at least one of the available Languages. 4. Optionally choose a preview image such as a PNG or JPEG. 5. Select Create theme. 6. When prompted, choose Open to open the code editor, if available. Creating a theme prepares workspace files and registers the new theme. Add components and page templates in the code editor before applying it to production. Import a packaged theme 1. In Import theme, choose Choose .zip file. 2. Select the approved BidoCMS theme archive. Selecting the archive starts the upload. 3. Review Theme import progress for validation, metadata and default-page updates, output generation, and activation. 4. After a successful import, allow the service to reconnect after its restart and check Publish → Publish Queue for the rebuild. 5. Review the language and page type mappings. Use History for the recorded source, outcome, and error details. Package import and theme publishing require the built-in CMS administrator. A delegated operator may be able to browse, create, and edit safe frontend files depending on role. If import fails, confirm the package uses the expected BidoCMS theme layout and review the specific validation error. What a packaged theme contains At the archive root, BidoCMS expects a setting.json file and a components/ directory. Include a scripts array in setting.json, even if the theme has no scripts. A component directory needs an HTML file with the same base name. The package can also include styles, images, fonts, scripts, and other theme assets. An optional image/theme.png supplies the gallery preview. Example component paths are components/StoryCard/StoryCard.html and components/StoryCard/StoryCard.css. Use a supported theme package structure when creating files in the editor. Keep deployment credentials in the server's environment configuration. Theme code editor · Deploy from Git · Map site page types

Connect and deploy a theme from Git Open Themes → Git repository with the built-in CMS administrator account to connect a theme's repository and branch. The integration reads a branch archive through its provider API and deploys it through BidoCMS theme import. Connect the repository 1. Select the Provider. Options include GitHub, GitLab, and self-hosted Gitea or Forgejo. Enter Server URL for a self-hosted provider when requested. 2. Sign in with GitHub when supported and configured, or use a provider access token. Use an account that can read the repository and manage its webhook when automatic registration is needed. 3. Select Show my repositories. Search or filter the list and select the repository. 4. Select the branch that holds the theme package files. 5. Review Deploy automatically on every push. Turn it off to record pushes for deployment on demand. 6. Select Connect this branch and confirm the repository and branch. 7. Select Deploy now when you want to import the current commit immediately. Connecting alone records the branch and attempts to register the push webhook. If GitHub sign-in asks for a client ID, complete the in-panel GitHub sign-in setup or use the access-token option. During device approval, use Open GitHub and Copy code to approve the request, then return to BidoCMS. Use the connected repository controls | Action | What it does | | --- | --- | | Deploy now | Confirms and starts an import for the connected branch. Watch Theme import progress and inspect History afterward. | | Check for new commits | Refreshes the latest branch information displayed in the status area. | | Deploy automatically on every push | Changes whether matching incoming pushes start deployment automatically. | | Change repository or branch | Reopens the connection wizard for a different target. | | Disconnect | Disconnects the repository and removes the managed webhook where possible. The saved sign-in can remain available for connecting another repository. | Diagnose a deployment or webhook Compare Latest commit seen with Last deployed commit. Review Last deployment, Last webhook received, and Last error before retrying. If BidoCMS could not register the webhook, follow the Add the push webhook by hand instructions for your provider, using the values shown for this connection. Keep the displayed webhook secret private. A branch package still needs to pass the import checks regardless of how deployment starts. Theme package import · Theme activity history

Theme activity history Open Themes → History to see recorded theme operations. The table can show ZIP uploads, Git imports, themes created in the panel, workspace operations, and republishes. | Column | What it shows | | --- | --- | | Status | Running, Success, Failed, or Interrupted. | | Source | Where the theme came from. | | Trigger | Manual, Git push, or Automatic. | | Details | Theme or archive name, or Git repository, branch, commit, and message. Errors appear here when supplied. | | By | The acting CMS user or Git commit author when available. | | Started | Start timestamp shown in the browser's local format. | | Duration | Recorded duration, or in progress for a running job. | Select Refresh to check the latest state. Use Older and Newer to navigate the records. The history table helps identify what changed. Use Publish → Publish Queue to monitor ordinary page generation. For Git, compare the commit in History with the connected branch's latest and last-deployed commit. For ZIP, verify that the archive is the intended BidoCMS package before trying again.
