Upload and manage agent packages Open AI & Agent → Upload agent to install an agent package and control its workspace. In this release, agent management and execution require an eligible CMS administrator with the Agents grant. Upload an agent 1. Open the Upload agent tab. 2. Choose the ZIP package. A valid package contains agent.json at its root and its declared JavaScript files. 3. Select Upload package. Uploading installs the program and does not start it. 4. In Installed agents, review the package name, version, description and Access line. These are declared by the package. 5. Switch the agent to Enabled to open its own workspace tab. Configure the inputs and verify the requirements in that workspace. A newly uploaded package starts disabled. If validation fails, check that the manifest is at the ZIP root, declared files exist, and all members use supported file types and paths. Change an existing installation | Task | What to do | | --- | --- | | Open the workspace | Select the enabled agent's named tab. | | See current installations | Use Refresh beside Installed agents. | | Pause an agent | Switch it to Disabled. This closes its workspace, prevents scheduled runs and cancels active execution. | | Update an agent | Upload a valid package with the same manifest ID. The updated agent is disabled. Compatible saved values with the same name and type are retained. Review and save the schedule again because the previous schedule is cleared. | | Review outputs after an update | Open the workspace and select an execution. Existing history is retained subject to the ten-run limit. | Package permissions allow the program to read the selected CMS capabilities and call configured tools. Review the source before installing packages, especially if they accept external credential inputs or make outbound provider requests. Run and schedule an agent · Package format reference

Agent package format and runtime requirements An agent package is a ZIP for AI & Agent → Upload agent. Its root contains agent.json and the JavaScript ES modules named by the manifest. An agent executes a bounded function with validated input and host-granted tools. ZIP and manifest - Root manifest fields are schemaVersion, id, name, version, description, permissions, inputs and functions. Optional fields are logo and requirements. Schema version is 1. - Give the package a stable lowercase ID, semantic version and readable description. Uploading the same ID updates the existing agent. - Each function declares its stable ID, display name, optional description, package-relative JavaScript file and exported function name. The runtime calls the export with (inputs, context). Return a JSON-compatible result. - Relative JavaScript imports must resolve inside the package. An optional PNG, JPEG or WebP logo can be bundled with the ZIP. - The importer rejects hidden paths, links, path traversal, duplicate or case-conflicting members and unsupported types. Include only intended package assets. There is no dependency installation step. Inputs, capabilities and prerequisites | Input type | Purpose | | --- | --- | | text, textarea | Short or longer string input. | | password | Masked external credential or other secret supplied by the administrator. | | number | Finite number with optional minimum and maximum. | | boolean | A checkbox value. False is a valid required selection. | | select | One declared option. | | ai | Selection of an existing enabled provider key and model. The package receives an identifier and model, and uses the declared input name for AI calls. | The host checks permissions separately from requirements. A requirement describes prerequisites and does not add tool access. Supported capability groups are site read, nodes read, Search Console read, Google Business read, generic public HTTP and AI generation. Corresponding requirement types are site, nodes, Search Console, Google Business, network, named input and AI. Required checks run before manual and scheduled execution. | Capability group | Host calls | | --- | --- | | Site | site.get | | Nodes | nodes.list, nodes.get, nodes.search | | Search Console | searchConsole.analytics, searchConsole.inspection | | Google Business | googleBusiness.locations, googleBusiness.profile | | Network | http.request | | AI | ai.generate | Use context.call(toolName, argumentsObject) for a declared tool and context.log(message) for non-sensitive progress. The isolated JavaScript runtime supplies standard language features, promises and package-relative imports. Built-in Node modules, direct filesystem access, direct fetch and arbitrary CMS writes are outside the provided interface. Limits The upload limit is 10 MiB and the total extracted package limit is 20 MiB. There can be at most 100 ZIP entries. The manifest supports up to 40 inputs and up to 20 functions. Individual runtime input and tool argument snapshots are limited to 64 KiB. A run can make up to 100 tool calls, with up to 10 concurrently and up to 10 AI calls. The normal CMS execution limit is two minutes. Install an agent package · Run and schedule an agent

Run an agent, schedule executions and export results Open the named workspace tab for the enabled agent in AI & Agent. Each installed package defines which functions, input fields and execution requirements appear in that workspace. Run the selected function 1. Choose a Function and read its description. 2. Fill in the input fields. For an AI input, select a saved key and compatible model. Password fields are masked. A blank optional password clears its value when the inputs are saved. 3. Check Execution requirements. Ready requirements allow the run. Required missing or unavailable dependencies block start. Optional requirements can appear as unmet while the run remains available. Use a setup link if shown, then recheck. 4. Choose Save inputs if the current inputs should be retained for a later run. 5. Choose Run now. The server checks current permission and required prerequisites again, then records the started execution in Recent executions. 6. Select View result to monitor a running execution or open a finished one. Closing the browser leaves server-side execution running. Run on a schedule 1. Select the function and fill in the inputs intended for scheduled use. 2. Expand Scheduled execution and check Enable schedule. 3. Enter a five-field Cron expression with minute, hour, day, month and weekday. For example, 0 9 * * 1 requests Monday at 09:00. 4. Enter an IANA Time zone, for example America/Vancouver. 5. Choose Save schedule and review Next run if shown. The schedule captures the function and inputs at the time you save it. Save the schedule again if those values need to change. 6. To remove a schedule, clear Enable schedule and choose Save schedule. Runs require the server to be running at the scheduled time. Downtime does not backfill missed executions. Only one run of an individual agent can execute at once. A started run can end as Completed, Failed or Stopped. A required preflight failure produces no execution record, and scheduled launch failures can be reflected on the schedule. Read and retain results Recent executions distinguishes Manual and Scheduled runs and reports timing and status. Use Execution log to check progress messages and Complete result to read the complete structured result. A tabular preview can show up to 100 rows and 30 columns. - Export Excel creates a workbook with execution details, logs and complete JSON. Tabular results also include a Results worksheet with bounded rows and columns. - Export JSON preserves the structured result. - The CMS retains the latest ten started executions per agent. Export a report you need beyond that retention window. Saved input snapshots are excluded from execution history and exports. Manage installed agents · Understand package inputs and requirements

Generate, edit and describe images with AI Image AI tools use credentials from AI & Agent → AI settings and save their results in the Images workspace. Each action displays only supported key and model combinations. Generate a new image 1. Open Images and navigate to the folder where the result belongs. 2. Use the AI image generation control to open Generate an image. 3. Select a saved API key and model, and enter Your prompt. 4. Optionally use the prompt-category dropdowns and supply an Action, Constraints or Image name. Read the assembled Final prompt before submitting. A prompt longer than 12,000 characters must be shortened. 5. Choose Aspect ratio from Square (1:1), Landscape (3:2) or Portrait (2:3). The Quality choices depend on the model and can be automatic. 6. Add reference images if the model supports them. References are ordered. The upload controls allow up to four reference uploads, 3 MiB for an individual file and 8 MiB combined. Some models allow fewer. 7. Select Generate image and wait for the new file to appear in the current folder. Requests can take a few minutes. Edit an existing image 1. Open the source image in the image editor. 2. Choose an enabled key for image editing and, if appropriate, select the area of interest. 3. Open Edit with AI, select the model and describe the change you want. For a masked edit, the original image and its mask are included automatically. Optional additional references follow the source. 4. Select Generate edited image. 5. Open the new image in the original folder and check the entire result. The selection guides the edit, and the model can change surrounding pixels for visual consistency. BidoCMS saves the entire result as a new image, keeping the original available. If the service asks you to retry after a response could not be received, repeat the action in the same dialog to retrieve the request safely. Generate alternative text, title and caption 1. Open the image's Details and choose the AI descriptions action. 2. Select a key and vision-capable model. 3. Review or edit the standard prompt. Use Reset to standard prompt to restore the default text. 4. Select Include website context if the optional context saved in Site → General should guide the descriptions. The panel enables the option initially when context exists. 5. Choose Generate and save for all languages. This writes the alternative text, title and caption for each configured website language. 6. Verify the visible descriptions and adjust the copy for the image's actual editorial use. If another editor changed the fields during generation, review the current values before retrying. Manage AI provider keys

Configure AI provider keys Open AI & Agent → AI settings to turn AI features on and manage named provider API keys. In an AI tool, pick the saved key and a compatible model for the requested action. Enable AI and add a key 1. Select Enable AI features and choose Save settings. 2. Under Provider API keys, locate Add an API key. 3. Enter a clear Key name, such as Editorial text or Marketing images. 4. Select the Provider. The capability list explains which actions the provider supports. Where available, use Manage [provider] API keys to reach its key console. 5. Paste the Provider API key. The form accepts 16–2,048 non-space characters. Choose Enable this key to make the key available for use. 6. Select Add key. The saved card displays its name, provider, a masked hint and Enabled or Disabled status. The provider catalog includes OpenAI, Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, xAI, Mistral AI, Groq, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Together AI, Fireworks AI, Cerebras, SambaNova and Cohere. The available model list is looked up against the selected key and filtered by action, so the same provider can show different choices for text, image generation, image editing or image descriptions. Edit, rotate or remove a saved key | Action | What happens | | --- | --- | | Edit → Save key | Change the name or enabled state. With the same provider, leave the secret field blank to keep the current value. | | Edit → change provider | Enter a key for the new provider before saving. | | Edit → enter a replacement key | Updates the credential while keeping its saved entry. Recheck any scheduled agents that depend on its model. | | Delete → Keep key | Closes the confirmation and keeps the saved credential. | | Delete → Delete key | Removes the saved credential. To use it again, add the key anew. | BidoCMS encrypts saved keys and shows only masked hints. The separate AI service receives the selected key for the provider request. The key can be used only within the supported actions. Provider billing and model access apply to AI requests. If a tool has no model choices Check that AI is enabled, the intended key is enabled, and the provider supports the operation. Use the model picker refresh control after changing provider credentials or account access. For image descriptions choose a key with a vision-capable model. If the AI service is temporarily unavailable, this panel can still let you manage saved keys. Use AI in an editor · Generate and edit images · Build theme components from Figma · Install an agent

Use AI in the rich-text editor Where the BidoCMS rich-text editor displays its AI action, it can answer a question about the current document or edit its content. The action uses saved AI credentials and an available text model. Work with a passage or the full document 1. Open the existing editor in the desired content language. 2. Select a passage first if the change should target only that text. 3. Open the editor's AI conversation and verify the Selected passage preview. Choose Remove in that preview to clear it and work with the document as a whole. 4. Select a saved credential and compatible model. Enter an instruction, such as “Shorten this paragraph to three sentences and preserve the booking link.” 5. Choose Send. Each message sends the full editor document and, if present, the marked passage to the chosen model. The instruction can be up to 6,000 characters. 6. Read the answer and check the editor. A reply-only answer does not replace content. An accepted edit may replace the selected passage or the complete editor document according to the instruction. 7. Use the surrounding editor's normal save workflow after reviewing the result. Follow the page's normal publishing workflow if the change should appear publicly. Revert or retry an edit - Use Revert AI edit to restore the preceding document when it still matches the AI revision. - If the editor says the document changed while waiting, review the latest content, select the passage again if needed and resend. - If unsupported markup prevented the edit, try a simpler change or select a smaller passage. - If the Send button is disabled, enter an instruction and select a compatible key and model. The button is also disabled while a request is pending. Manage AI provider keys

Compare Search Console, Google Analytics and URL Inspection BidoCMS has several Google reporting views. Choose one by the question you want to answer. The reports use different event definitions, dates and scopes, so matching totals should not be expected. | Question | Workspace | Scope | | --- | --- | --- | | What queries, countries or devices produced Google Search clicks for this page? | Pages → Analytics → Performance | Selected localized page scope and Google search type. | | Did a page receive traffic from Discover? | Pages → Analytics → Discover | The page's Google Discover activity where Google returns sufficient data. | | Which sessions, events and engagement did GA4 record for this page? | Pages → Analytics → Analytics | The localized page path and matching GA4 website streams in the selected property. | | How many users were active on the website recently? | Notifications → Google Analytics live | Realtime active users for matching website streams in the selected GA4 property. | | Has Google indexed the localized URL, and which canonical does it use? | Pages → Search Engines | Google's stored inspection for the exact localized public URL. | Compare dates and filters Search Console archive dates use Pacific time. The GA4 page report uses the selected property's reporting time zone and excludes today. The realtime card uses rolling windows in minutes. Before comparing reports, record the selected date range, time zone, page language and filters. Search Console measures activity in Google surfaces. GA4 measures activity it recorded on the website. Traffic sources beyond Google Search can appear in GA4. Search Console can attribute traffic to a canonical URL, and GA4 data can vary with tag setup, measurement settings and visitors' consent choices. Investigate a missing report 1. Check whether the expected provider connection is active under Settings → Search Console or Settings → Analytics. 2. In Pages, select the intended language and check the displayed public URL, including the locale prefix or trailing slash. 3. Check the available report source, range, filters and provider notes. 4. For recent publication or canonical changes, use Search Engines and compare Google's last crawl with the publication timing. 5. For historical search traffic, check the archive coverage. For GA4 traffic, verify the selected property and compare the public tracking stream in GA4. Read Search Console data · Read historical GA4 · Read realtime GA4 · Inspect indexing status

Read a page's Google Analytics report Open Pages → selected page → selected language → Analytics, then choose Analytics in the report selector. The Google Analytics report shows historical GA4 activity for this page's public URL and matching streams. Use it to compare traffic, engagement and events over time. Read the page overview 1. Verify the displayed Page URL and selected language. 2. Choose 7 days, 28 days, 90 days, 180 days, 365 days, or Custom dates and Apply. The end date is yesterday or earlier in the property's reporting time zone. A custom period can contain up to 365 days. 3. The Page overview compares totals with the immediately preceding period of the same length. Select a metric card to explore the daily chart. 4. Focus the chart and use Left or Right arrow keys to examine each day, or choose View chart data for the daily values in a table. 5. Choose Open in Analytics to work with the Google property directly when needed. | Metric | Meaning | | --- | --- | | Active users | Active users in the selected URL scope. | | Views | Page views, including repeat views. | | Sessions | Sessions attributed to the selected URL scope by the GA4 report. | | New users | Users reported as new by GA4. | | Average engagement time per active user | Engagement duration divided by active users. | | Engagement rate | Reported share of engaged sessions. | | Event count | Tracked event occurrences. | | Key events | Events configured as key events in GA4. | | Total revenue | Revenue reported by GA4 for this scope. Google account restrictions may make it unavailable. | Period totals are queried separately. In particular, adding daily or group-by user counts, sessions or rates can give a different result. Break down and export results Switch between Session channel group, Session source / medium, Country, City, Device category, Browser, Page path + query string and Event name. Depending on the chosen breakdown, select headings to sort, use Search table to filter the returned rows, and change Rows per page to navigate the results. At most the top 1,000 provider rows are returned. If Google reports truncation, the panel identifies the limit. Export CSV includes the selected URL and dates, current and previous totals, daily data, and the current table with its search filter applied. The displayed page of the table is used for navigation. Export includes the available filtered rows. Interpret missing data - Confirm the site stream and page URL if all metrics are missing. A shared GA4 property is filtered by both the matched streams and the localized public URL. - Recent GA4 historical data can take 24–48 hours to complete processing. - Check the quality notes when Google reports privacy thresholds, sampling or the (other) grouping. - Distinguish restricted revenue from a reported zero. Check Google Analytics property permissions if the report says revenue is unavailable. - For current active users across the installation's matched streams, use the Google Analytics live card in Notifications. Set up the GA4 connection · Read Search Console data for the same page

Read page performance and Discover data Open Pages, select a page and its content language, then choose Analytics. In the report selector choose Performance for Google Search traffic or Discover for Google Discover. The corresponding views require an active Search Console connection and access to the selected page. Select a period and search type 1. Verify the displayed page URL and selected content language. 2. Choose a date preset, such as 7 days, 28 days or 3 months, or open More to choose other ranges including Full archive. Choose More → Custom to enter your own dates. Search Console dates use Pacific time for Search Console data. 3. In Performance, choose the search type that applies to the question: Web (text), Image, Video, News or Google News. 4. Use the metric cards to show or hide Total clicks, Total impressions, Average CTR and Average position on the chart. Clicks and impressions are selected initially. Choose daily, weekly or monthly chart aggregation. 5. If available, inspect data availability and finalization information below the controls. The report can include finalized data, dotted preliminary data and gaps for unavailable dates. | Metric | How to interpret it | | --- | --- | | Clicks | Clicks from the chosen Google source to the selected page scope. | | Impressions | Appearances for that scope as counted by Google. | | CTR | Clicks divided by impressions. | | Average position | Position weighted by impressions when days are rolled up. It is available in Performance. | Discover uses its own data and only shows clicks, impressions and CTR. Switch between views when investigating a change specific to Google Search or Discover. Read details and drill down Performance offers Queries, Pages, Countries, Devices, Search appearance and Days. Discover offers Pages, Countries, Discover appearance and Days. - Select a column header to sort available rows and use the table controls to review more rows. - Select a row to filter the report by that row's value. A query selection opens a Pages view for that query. A CMS administrator can see matching paths on the verified installation hosts. A delegated user remains within pages their role can access. - A Pages row is an actual URL Google returned, including its query string or www hostname where applicable. Selecting the row applies that exact URL. Choosing a Day applies the corresponding date or date range. - Remove a filter individually or choose Reset filters to return to the selected page's normal report. - Use Export to download the current breakdown and selected metric columns as CSV. Record the active source, date range and filters when sharing results. Match the data to the right URL The report follows the selected page's saved URL and language. It groups eligible base and www hostname variants and optional query strings on the verified site. Paths remain case sensitive, and different language paths and trailing-slash paths can represent separate scopes. With a URL-prefix property, Google's coverage is limited to that property. If Google attributes the clicks to another canonical URL, available metrics may appear on that canonical page. Use Search Engines to check what Google selected. Understand gaps and empty reports The background collector imports and refreshes site data independently of opening the report. Connecting a new site starts collection for available history, and more ranges and breakdowns may appear later. Collection can mark confirmed zeroes separately from dates that are still missing. Private or high-cardinality query rows can be withheld by Google, so adding query rows may produce a lower figure than the chart. A low-volume page can also have insufficient data for a Discover report even when it has Search traffic. Connect Search Console · Understand the Search Console archive · Inspect the indexed URL

Read Search Console archive coverage and daily collection status The Performance and Discover reports under Pages → Analytics use an archive collected by the central Search Console service. Opening either report reads available records. Collection continues in the background for published language URLs. Recognize coverage states | Status or pattern | Meaning | | --- | --- | | Figures for X of Y days | The chart has available figures for X days in the requested range. | | Blank segment in the chart | No available observation for that segment. This is different from a confirmed zero. | | Dotted chart segment | Preliminary figures can still change. | | Site data finalized through | Google's finalization point for site data when provided. | | Site totals checked | The last available site totals check shown by the service. | | Fewer covered days under a table | This breakdown is still collecting or has less available detail than the chart. | | Top rows available from Search Console | Google can omit certain queries or return a limited breakdown. | The initial background import covers the available Google history and prioritizes recent reports. More → Full archive includes retained data that has already been collected, which can extend beyond the provider's moving history window. Data can appear in batches, so the chart and its breakdown tables can fill at different times. Check a newly connected or newly published page 1. In Settings → Search Console, check the active property and verification status. 2. In Pages, open the intended language variant and verify its saved public URL and publication state. 3. Reopen Analytics → Performance, use a recent date range and review the archive coverage. If the chart has data, check the detail coverage for the relevant breakdown separately. 4. Open Search Engines for Google's stored index state, canonical decision and last crawl. If the first examination is pending, use the available manual inspection action when needed. 5. If opening the same search report later still shows incomplete coverage, record the property, public URL, language, report source, date range and the visible coverage messages when asking the administrator to check collection. Connection and reconnection start collection for the active property. Scheduled data collection checks recent and unresolved dates in Pacific time. The service keeps observations already collected when reports are temporarily unavailable. Disconnecting hides the archive until the corresponding property and access scope are verified again. Read a page's search report · Connect Search Console

Connect Bido SEO and trusted applications through CMS OAuth Open Settings → OAuth as a CMS administrator to control which trusted applications can use delegated read access. This workflow lets an eligible CMS user grant an application, such as Bido SEO, access to the approved site and page read scopes. Register and authorize Bido SEO 1. In the Bido SEO project, open Connections → Add connection, choose CMS connection, and enter the site's final HTTPS URL. 2. Copy the exact redirect URL Bido SEO displays, including its connection query parameter. 3. In BidoCMS, open Settings → OAuth → Registered applications → Add application. 4. Set Application name, optionally add a Description, and paste the full redirect into Exact callback URLs. 5. Keep the application enabled and select both site and page read permissions, shown as site:read and nodes:read. 6. Choose Eligible CMS administrators only or Only selected CMS people. For the second option, use Find a CMS person to locate and select eligible accounts. Their site and page permissions are still checked. 7. Save the application. Copy the displayed client ID and one-time client secret into Bido SEO. The client secret is shown once and can be cleared from the panel. If it is lost, rotate it to get a new value. 8. In Connection details, copy the CMS authorization URL, token URL and connector API base URL into the Bido SEO connection. Depending on the client, the revocation endpoint may also be needed. 9. If OAuth is disabled, select Enable OAuth access, choose the lifetimes, and use Save access policy. 10. In Bido SEO, choose Authorize CMS. Sign in with an eligible CMS account and approve after reviewing the application, callback and requested scopes. Return to Bido SEO and sync. Review access policy and applications | Setting or action | Behavior | | --- | --- | | Enable OAuth access | Enables authorization for registered, enabled apps when a trusted public HTTPS issuer is configured. | | Access token lifetime (seconds) | Accepts 300–3,600 seconds. The initial policy value is 900 seconds. | | Refresh token lifetime (days) | Accepts 1–90 days. The initial policy value is 30 days. | | Exact callback URLs | Supply one HTTPS URL per line, up to 10, with any query string included. Wildcards and fragments are rejected. | | Application enabled | Controls whether that registered application may authorize and retain access. | | Edit application | Changes the application's settings. Security-relevant changes can revoke current authorizations. | | Rotate client secret | Generates a replacement credential and invalidates existing authorizations for the application. Update the application and authorize again. | | Revoke application access | Disables this application and revokes its connections. | | Revoke connection | Stops the selected connection in Authorized connections. | Saving a changed access policy can require all existing applications to authorize again. Check Authorized connections for the authorizing CMS person, scopes, authorization date, last use and expiration. Resolve authorization errors If Enable OAuth access is unavailable, the server needs a trusted issuer for the site. If a redirect is rejected, copy the full current URL from the relevant Bido SEO connection and compare the path and query string exactly. If the consent page blocks an account, check the authorized people setting and the account's current read permissions. Sign-in alone does not approve the grant. For reporting integrations managed through Google's consent screen, use Search Console or Google Analytics.

Connect a Facebook Page and manage posts or messages Open Social → Facebook to manage Facebook Pages available to the website. Posts, Inbox and Profile are scoped to the selected Page. Connect and verify your Page 1. Choose Connect Facebook and sign in to an account that manages the intended Page. 2. Approve the relevant Facebook permissions and choose the Pages you want to connect. One CMS installation can connect multiple Facebook Pages. 3. Select the Page tab and open Profile. Check the displayed identity and status, and optionally choose Open on Facebook. 4. Use Refresh profile to update the displayed information. Use Add Facebook Page to connect another Page, Reconnect Facebook to renew authorization, or Disconnect to remove the selected CMS connection. Publish and manage posts 1. In Posts, choose Create post if publishing access is available. 2. Enter Post text. Optionally choose one Link, one Public image URL or one Photo upload. The URL must use HTTPS and Facebook must be able to fetch the image. 3. For a photo upload, select one JPEG or PNG, up to 5 MB. 4. Confirm the target Page and choose Publish post. 5. Use Refresh posts, then open the resulting post to review details. If the provider and Page grant allow it, Edit post updates the text and Delete post removes the post from Facebook. In post details, Comments can show existing comments. Use the available reply, hide, show or delete controls according to the Page's permissions. A visible post does not imply moderation access. Read and respond to Page messages Open Inbox, select a conversation and review its messages. Use Load older messages to browse backward and the relevant refresh control for the conversation list or thread. If Facebook permits a response and the Page has message write permission, type the reply and choose Send reply. An app pending setup or an account missing provider access can limit a section. Check the Meta app configuration, CMS submenu grant and Page role. If a single thread is unavailable for replies, read the reason displayed in that thread. Return to Social workspace guide

Connect Google Analytics 4 Open Settings → Analytics to connect BidoCMS to an existing Google Analytics 4 property. The integration reads GA4 data for page reports and the Google Analytics live card in Notifications. Installing the website's tracking tag and collecting new GA4 events are separate steps. Before you connect - The Google account needs at least Viewer access to the target GA4 property. - The property needs a web data stream whose default URL matches the installation's public HTTPS hostname or its www equivalent at the root. - Your CMS role needs Settings → Google Analytics. The tab in the Settings workspace is labeled Analytics. - The central GA4 integration must be available so BidoCMS can discover properties and read reports. Connect, change property or check access 1. Open Settings → Analytics and verify the site address. 2. Select Connect Google Analytics. 3. Sign in to the account that can access the site's property and allow read access on Google's consent screen. 4. Back in the panel, confirm Connected and check Property, Time zone and Measurement ID. When there are multiple matching properties, BidoCMS initially picks the matching property with the lowest numeric ID. 5. Use Change property, select the matching GA4 property for this website, then select Use property. BidoCMS rechecks access when saving the selection. 6. Use Check access to reverify the selected property, or Reconnect with Google to renew consent. A rejected or cancelled reconnection preserves a previously saved grant. Disconnect removes the Analytics connection and its report cache. Search Console and Google Business have separate connections. Realtime and historical data The Notifications card uses the selected property's realtime report for matching web streams. It reflects recent activity reported by GA4. An unavailable connection or a provider error is reported separately from a successful response with zero active users. The analytical reports under Pages → Analytics → Analytics use historical page data through yesterday in the property's reporting time zone and can show different values from the realtime card. Troubleshoot the connection | Panel message or symptom | What to check | | --- | --- | | Google account does not have Analytics access to this website | Check Google Analytics access in the browser and confirm Viewer or higher access to the correct property and the matching stream URL. | | Expected property is missing | Compare the website's root domain and stream default URL, and make sure the same Google account has the intended property listed. | | Enable the Analytics Admin and Data APIs | Ask the central service operator to verify that both Google APIs are enabled. | | Allow Google Analytics access | Repeat consent and approve Analytics read access. | | Service unavailable or site verification fails | Verify the installation's public HTTPS address and ask the administrator to check the central service if the issue persists. | | The live card is connected and shows zero | Check realtime traffic in the selected GA4 property and confirm that the website's tracking tag is configured and receiving traffic. | Read the individual page report

Connect Google Business and select locations Open Social → Google Business to manage Google Business Profile locations the connected Google account owns or manages. Connect, choose a business and select the branch 1. Select Connect Google and complete Google's authorization using the account that manages the Business Profile. 2. After consent, choose Choose business. Review the businesses and branches returned by Google. 3. Select one business and choose Connect this business. The CMS can then manage that business’s returned locations. 4. When the business has more than one returned location, choose the correct Branch before editing, replying to a review or publishing. 5. Switch between available locations with the branch picker. To choose a different business, disconnect the current Google Business connection and complete the connection and selection again. A connected Google account may return several businesses and locations. CMS submenu grants and provider permissions both affect which features appear. Google may require a verified location for reviews and posts. Connection recovery - If account setup or the app is pending, check with the BidoCMS administrator. Authorizing requires the provider app to be provisioned and the intended Google account to have permission. - If the business is absent, verify you signed in as its owner or manager, and use Reload locations where offered. - If authorization expired, choose Reconnect Google. - Select Disconnect to remove this site's Google Business connection. The Business Profile remains in Google. The workspace uses Google Business Profile. For its settings and reporting functions use the branch tabs. Maps embedded in a website theme and the page-level Google Search Console and Analytics connections are separate features. Edit profile, hours, services and attributes · Manage reviews and posts · Manage photos, links and performance

Reply to Google reviews and publish business updates Use Social → Google Business and select the intended branch before working in Reviews or Posts. Google can require a verified profile and sufficient account permissions. Read reviews and respond 1. Open Reviews and find the review for this branch. Choose Load more to read further results as available. 2. Open the reply controls and write or edit the business response. 3. Choose Publish reply for a first reply or Save reply after editing one. It is attached to the original review on Google. 4. Use Delete reply only if you intend to remove that business response. Use the Google review management tools to report an issue with the review itself. Create a post or share a published page 1. Choose Posts → Create post. 2. Select Post type for a new post or a published-page share. 3. For a published-page share, use Search published pages and Find pages. Select the intended Published page, then check the suggested text, language and read-only link. 4. Review Post text. A new post can include Link (optional for a new post). A publicly reachable picture from the site can be specified in Public photo URL from this site (optional). 5. Review Post language, for example en or fr-CA, and the selected branch. 6. Choose Publish on Google, then View posts when available to check the provider result. The provider can mark a post Published, Processing or Rejected by Google. Open a post to see available actions. Edit text changes the post summary where supported. Delete post removes the selected update from Google after confirmation. If a CMS page is absent from the picker, confirm that the desired language version has a public published URL. Checking saved edits in Pages alone does not add a page to the published chooser. Choose a location · Open performance and marketing tools

Manage Google Business photos, action links and performance Open a branch in Social → Google Business. Photos, Bookings & links, Performance and Google tools cover the branch's public media, actions and selected statistics. Photos 1. Open Photos → Add a photo. 2. Enter Public image URL from this site and choose a Photo category. 3. Choose Add photo to Google. Use a URL that the provider can fetch publicly. 4. Review the provider's returned media cards. Use Delete media and confirm if an existing item should be removed from Google. Bookings and action links 1. Open Bookings & links. 2. To create an action, use Add an action link and choose a supported Link type. 3. Enter the Destination URL and select Preferred link if this action should be marked preferred. 4. Choose Save link. Open an existing action for its update controls, or use Delete link to remove it. Google's Place Actions capability controls availability. An action link connects visitors to a destination such as a booking URL and does not add a bookings calendar to the CMS. Performance and Google tools Performance shows the last 30 days returned by Google for the selected branch. Read the displayed start and end dates and the total for each metric. Returned metrics can include impressions and user actions such as direction requests or bookings. Empty metrics can mean Google had no data to return for that branch and period. If the panel indicates that the Performance API is unavailable, ask the administrator to check the central Google integration. Use Google tools to open Google Business Profile Manager or Manage review reports. Google's own workspace is the destination for product catalog, ads, account permissions and other management tools. Connect Google Business

Edit Google Business profile, hours, attributes and services Go to Social → Google Business and select the correct branch. The sections save changes to that Google location. Available fields depend on the location type and returned provider data. Profile 1. Open Profile. 2. Review Business name, Website, Primary phone and Business description. 3. When Storefront address is displayed, review street address, city, province or state, and postal code. The form shows the country separately. 4. In Business categories, choose a Primary category. To add an available category, enter a query under Find a category, select Find categories, pick an item in Google categories and use Add selected category. Remove additional categories with their named controls. 5. Where editable, use Business status to switch between open and temporarily closed. 6. Select Save profile. The panel sends changed fields. No changes to save indicates the displayed values match the loaded profile. When Google provides the links, Open business on Maps, Open review link and Copy review link are available here. Hours - Under Weekly hours, add or edit an opening period with Open day, Close day, Opens (HH:MM) and Closes (HH:MM). Choose Save weekly hours. - Under Special and holiday hours, choose Add special date, enter the date and optional end date, then set the opening and closing time or Closed all day. Choose Save special hours. - Use Remove on a row before saving the updated hours if that period should be removed. The weekly and special hours forms save independently. Review both when making a holiday change. Attributes and services | Tab | Workflow | | --- | --- | | Attributes | Review the location's editable attributes. Change the desired values and choose Save attributes. Attributes come from the provider and can depend on categories and location. | | Services | Review structured and custom services, edit available descriptions, and use Add service where categories permit it. For a custom service enter Service name, Category and Description. Remove rows as needed and choose Save services. | If the provider refuses a change or a field is absent, check the selected branch and the permissions and categories on the Google profile. Reload the branch if someone else may have edited it since the form opened. Connect Google Business and select a branch

Connect Instagram and manage account sections Open Social → Instagram to connect a supported account through Meta. Each connected account has its own media, inbox and settings. Select its account tab before working. Connect or renew an account 1. Choose Connect Instagram and complete the Meta authorization flow using the account you intend to manage. 2. If the browser blocks the authorization window, allow it for this site and start again. Wait for the completion message. 3. Choose the connected account. To manage more accounts, use Add Instagram account. 4. Open Profile and verify Username, Connection and Access expires. Use Refresh account to reread the current profile or Reconnect Instagram when authorization is needed again. 5. To change the label that appears in the CMS, edit Account name in this panel and choose Save name. 6. If an account should no longer be connected, select it and use Disconnect, then confirm the account name. Find media, stories and insights | Section | What you can do | | --- | --- | | Posts | Browse accessible posts, open media details, review comments and start Create post when the account can publish. | | Reels | Open published reels and available details for them. | | Inbox | Read available conversations and reply with the account's messaging permissions. | | Profile | Review the connection, CMS label and expiry. | | Active stories | Open active stories from Profile when that permission is available. Roles without Profile access may see Stories as a separate tab if granted. | | Account insights | Open insights from Profile when available, or use the Insights tab if your role exposes it directly. | For account insights, select Metric, optionally set From and To, and choose Load insights. Available metrics in the form include Reach, Views, Profile views and Followers. Individual media can expose its own Insights action depending on provider capability. If the report is empty, check the metric, period and account access. If connection setup is unavailable, the installation's Instagram integration may still require provisioning. If the account can publish but Posts does not show existing content, media reading requires its own provider access. Publish or schedule Instagram media · Handle comments and messages

Manage Instagram comments and conversations Use the selected account's Posts, Reels or Inbox section in Social → Instagram. Reading comments or conversations and performing actions can require different Meta capabilities. Review or moderate media comments 1. Open the account's media list and select a post or reel. 2. Open the available comments view and choose Load more comments where needed. 3. For a reply, find the intended comment, open Reply, write your response and choose Send reply. 4. Use the available hide, show or delete actions according to the comment and the account's moderation capability. Read the confirmation carefully before deleting. Read and reply from Inbox 1. Open Inbox and check the account identity. 2. Select the conversation. Use Load more conversations or Load older messages if the entry you need is outside the current results. 3. If the account can send messages and the provider permits a reply in the conversation, enter the reply and send it. Use the supported photo attachment action if the composer offers it. 4. Check the thread after sending. Use the view's refresh control if the provider response and displayed thread are temporarily out of sync. If Inbox is absent, verify the CMS submenu grant and the account's messaging capability. If you can read a conversation but cannot send, check the conversation's current eligibility and the account's send permission. Follow the message shown for the active conversation. Connect the account · Publish Instagram posts

Draft, publish and schedule Instagram posts Open Social → Instagram and select the intended account. Under Posts, choose Create post. This action is available to users and accounts with publishing access. Prepare a publication 1. Select Format: Image, Carousel, Reel or Story. The available list depends on your CMS grants. 2. Add the Caption. The panel accepts up to 2,200 characters. For story text that should appear in the media itself, include it in the uploaded image or video. 3. Select files under Upload media, then Upload selected files. Choose them in the intended display order. Alternatively expand Use a media URL from this website, enter a same-site HTTPS Media URL, choose Media type and select Add media URL. 4. Review each uploaded item. Add Alternative text to eligible images, and remove or replace any expired upload. 5. If you want a draft, optionally enter Draft name and choose Save draft. Resume from Saved drafts → Open draft. Choose New draft to reset the composer. 6. Leave Schedule empty to select Publish now. To schedule, enter a future time in the browser time zone shown and select Schedule publication. 7. Check Publication history for the current state. Uploading assets and submitting them can precede the published result. Format checks and troubleshooting | Format | Required media | | --- | --- | | Image | One image. | | Carousel | At least two items and up to 20 from the composer. Media can contain images or videos. | | Reel | One video. | | Story | One compatible media item. | The composer accepts JPEG, PNG, WebP, MP4 and QuickTime where the selected format and provider accept them. An expired temporary upload must be removed and uploaded again. The composer accepts a future date for scheduling. Published caption editing is unavailable in this composer, so verify the caption before submitting. | Publication history action | When to use it | | --- | --- | | Cancel | Stop an eligible preparing, queued or scheduled item before publication begins. | | Check publication | Ask for confirmation on a submitted item. Submission means Instagram received the request. | | Record as published | For an uncertain result, first verify the post on Instagram and then enter its published media ID. | | Confirm not published | For an uncertain result, first confirm on Instagram that no post was created. | | Copy caption to new draft | Reuse the caption from a failed or cancelled entry. Upload the media for the new draft. | A submitted or processing state can still be awaiting the provider. Check the existing history entry and the Instagram account before submitting a duplicate. Manage the connected Instagram account · Handle comments and messages

Connect a LinkedIn profile or company Page Open Social → LinkedIn. The managed workspace opens an account's Posts and Profile together. Installations connected to a separate LinkedIn service can show additional workspace tabs. Connect and select a profile 1. Choose Connect LinkedIn and complete LinkedIn authorization. 2. For company Pages, sign in to a member account with appropriate Page roles. Company Page discovery and reading may require LinkedIn Community Management access in the service's app. 3. After authorization, choose the intended personal profile or company Page when several identities are listed. 4. In Profile, check the account status, capability tags and Page roles when shown. Use Sync to refresh profile details, roles and scopes. New company Page discovery can require another LinkedIn authorization. 5. To add another identity, choose Add LinkedIn account where available. To restore an expired or revoked identity, choose Reconnect LinkedIn. Disconnect removes the selected local account connection.
