Use Posts and Profile in the managed workspace - Open Posts and choose Create post if the selected profile or Page has publishing access. Publish as is the selected identity. Enter Commentary, up to 3,000 characters, optionally choose Disable resharing, and select Publish now. The managed composer uses text posts. - An account with read access shows available LinkedIn posts and Refresh posts. BidoCMS publication history shows submissions made from the CMS for this account, including for publish-only accounts. - Review Details on a history entry. Submitted indicates LinkedIn accepted a post identifier. Final visibility can be confirmed with Verify on LinkedIn when read access is available. - A successful post can offer Edit post or Delete from LinkedIn according to its permissions. Editing changes the LinkedIn post text. Deleting removes the provider post and retains its local history state. If a feature is unavailable Publishing, reading, media and engagement are separate provider capabilities. Compare the account's visible capabilities and Page role with the attempted action. If LinkedIn app setup is pending, check with the administrator responsible for the installation. Use the separate LinkedIn service workspace · Return to the Social overview

Use LinkedIn service settings, publishing, media and activity Some installations expose the standalone LinkedIn service workspace under Social → LinkedIn. The visible tabs depend on CMS access and the service integration. | Section | What it provides | | --- | --- | | Overview | Service status, connection details, account and recent publication counts, and Panel connection settings. | | Accounts | Member authorizations, member and organization identities, account sync and disconnect. | | Publish | Composer and stored publication jobs. | | Content | Posts and engagement tools for identities with the corresponding provider permissions. | | Media | Uploaded or remote reusable publication assets. | | Activity | Jobs, Events and Audit records for the service. | Check the service settings In Overview, use Refresh to reread the connection and recent provider results. In Panel connection settings, review Connection name and Service URL. When the URL is pinned by configuration the field is disabled. Save settings verifies the configuration. Remove integration detaches the website from the service and can suspend the tenant while retaining service data. Queue a publication 1. Open Publish. Choose Publish as from active publishing identities. 2. Select a Publication type, such as Text, Article, Image, Multiple images, Video, Document or Reshare. Enter Commentary and complete the media or article fields shown for that type. 3. Optionally enter Schedule (optional) for future publication and choose Disable resharing if appropriate. 4. Select Queue publication. In the publication list, choose Details to see the state and any provider message. 5. Use Cancel for a scheduled item that has not started, or Verify on LinkedIn on a supported submitted item. If the service requires reconciliation, verify the provider state before choosing the corresponding Mark published or Mark failed action. 6. For a failed, cancelled or deleted entry, Use as template copies its content into a new publication; review the resulting identity and fields before queueing it. Work with media, content and activity Use Media → Upload a file to upload an eligible image, video or document through the CMS. To keep an external source for a later publication, open Register a remote URL, enter Remote media URL and optionally MIME type, then choose Save remote media. The service stores the asset reference for the composer. In Content, use the account and post controls you have available to read posts and manage engagement. A Page's approved LinkedIn app permissions determine which comment and reaction actions are available. In Activity, choose Jobs for execution status, Events for outbound delivery records or Audit for operation details. This is service activity. To investigate a publication, begin with its publication history and inspect the corresponding job or event if needed. Connect a LinkedIn account

Connect Google Search Console Open Settings → Search Console to connect the public website to a Google Search Console property. This connection enables Search Console performance and Discover reports, along with Google URL Inspection in page workspaces. Before you connect - Use a Google account that already has access to the website's property in Search Console. - Check that the public site address displayed in Settings uses HTTPS and belongs to this installation. The CMS must be able to verify its public website. - Your CMS role must include Settings → Search Console. Viewing reports uses separate page permissions. - A Domain property can cover both the base and www hostname. A URL-prefix property is limited to the prefix Google granted. BidoCMS selects a verified property and displays which one it uses. Connect and verify access 1. Open Settings → Search Console. 2. Check the website address in the connection card. 3. Select Connect Search Console. Google opens its sign-in and consent screen. 4. Select the Google account with access to this website and approve the requested Search Console read access. 5. Back in BidoCMS, confirm the Connected badge. Check Property, Access and Last verified. Access can be Owner, Full user or Restricted user according to Google's grant. 6. Select Check access if you need to confirm that the account can still read the property. BidoCMS saves the connection after Google verifies access to the displayed website. The connection reads existing data. Reconnect or disconnect Use Reconnect with Google if access expired, the Google account changed, or the panel displays Reconnect needed. Complete consent before checking reports. A cancelled or failed reconnect preserves the previously saved connection. Use Disconnect and confirm to hide Search Console reports. The installation keeps the archive and can make it available again after matching property and access scope are verified on reconnection. Google Analytics is managed separately under Settings → Analytics. If you cannot connect | Panel message or symptom | What to check | | --- | --- | | Account has no Search Console access to this website | Sign in to Search Console directly, confirm the property is visible under the intended account, and restart consent with that account. | | Allow Search Console access | Approve the permission on Google's consent screen. | | Set the public HTTPS website address | Ask the site administrator to check the configured public site address. | | The service could not verify this website | Verify that the configured HTTPS website is publicly reachable and points to the correct installation. | | The central Google service is awaiting setup | Ask the BidoCMS administrator about service configuration, then choose Refresh status. | | The connection changed in another session | Refresh the connection state and start the action again. | Understand page search performance · Inspect a page's index status

Find and open a Social workspace Open Social to manage the connected profiles and business locations supported by your installation. Work takes place inside the selected provider, and where multiple profiles or branches exist, inside the selected identity. Choose a provider | Provider | Where to work | | --- | --- | | Google Business | Business and branch selection, Profile, Hours, Attributes, Reviews, Posts, Photos, Services, Bookings & links, Performance and Google tools. | | Facebook | Connected Facebook Pages with Posts, Inbox and Profile. | | Instagram | Connected Instagram accounts with Posts, Reels, Inbox and Profile, plus Stories and Insights where allowed. | | X (Twitter) | Connected X accounts with Posts, Inbox and Profile. | | LinkedIn | Connected profiles and Pages. Managed installations show Posts and Profile for the selected account. Other installations may expose a service workspace with Overview, Accounts, Publish, Content, Media and Activity. | | Telegram | Coming soon in this panel version. | | WhatsApp | Coming soon in this panel version. | Check identity, permission and connection status 1. Click the provider tab. 2. For providers with several connected accounts, confirm the selected account or Page. Google Business uses a selected business and, where applicable, a branch picker. 3. Use the provider's Profile or Overview to check current connection and available capabilities. Connection setup or reconnect may require a different CMS role. 4. Choose the content, inbox, reporting or settings section you need. Before publishing or replying, confirm the account and resulting destination. A role may grant access to Social without granting every provider or every submenu. A provider may require a configured app, approved scopes or an eligible profile type for specific features. If the workspace shows app setup is pending, ask the BidoCMS administrator to check provisioning. If a connected account needs authorization again, use its provider-specific reconnect control. If the same section works for another account, compare the two accounts' provider scopes and roles before changing the CMS role. Google Business · Facebook · Instagram · LinkedIn · X

Connect an X account and manage posts or conversations Open Social → X (Twitter) to work with the selected connected X identity. The panel offers Posts, Inbox and Profile when role and provider permissions allow. Connect or refresh an X account 1. Choose Connect X and complete the X sign-in and consent flow. 2. Check Profile for the connected name and current status. Use Open on X when offered to verify the remote profile. 3. To manage another identity, use Add X account and select its account tab after authorization. 4. Use Refresh profile to reread account data or Reconnect X if authorization expired. Disconnect removes the selected account's local connection. Publish and manage posts 1. Open Posts and select Create post if your account can publish. 2. Enter Post text, up to 280 characters in the composer. With the media permission, attach one JPEG, PNG or WebP image up to 5 MB. Links can be included in the text. 3. Verify the active account and select Publish post. 4. Use Refresh posts, then open the relevant post to see the provider URL and any available replies or management actions. Replies are shown when the provider grants readable replies. Replying, moderating or deleting requires the corresponding capability and an eligible item. If the panel does not show an edit action, use the operations currently available for the post. Check the inbox Open Inbox, select a conversation and use Load older messages to read previous messages. Use the inbox and thread refresh actions when needed. The reply field appears when both the account grant and conversation allow it. Choose Send reply to respond from the selected account. If Posts or Inbox reports insufficient access, check the app permissions and reconnect with the appropriate scopes if they are available for this installation's X app. In some cases the provider's API cannot return an individual message or support a thread action. The panel displays the returned limitation. Return to Social workspace guide

Configure email notifications and account email Open Settings → General and locate Notification Enable and Method. This configuration supplies the installation's outgoing mail transport. Account recovery and email delivery of temporary passwords depend on a configured mail transport. Monitor alert rules use their own recipient lists. Choose a method | Method | Values to prepare | | --- | --- | | Normal | SMTP Host, Port, sender email in username, and the authorized SMTP password in password. | | Sendgrid | SendGrid SMTP Host and Port, authorized sender email in username, and API key in password. BidoCMS uses apikey as the SMTP authentication username. | | Gmail | The Gmail sender email and the credential authorized for SMTP access. The Gmail transport provides its own service settings. | | Gmail Relay | A sender email and a Google Workspace SMTP relay configured for the server. BidoCMS uses the Gmail relay host on port 587. | | Postmark | The authorized Sender email address and Postmark server API token. The form hides Host and Port for this mode and saves Postmark's SMTP address on port 587. | Save and check delivery 1. Turn on Notification Enable. 2. Select the Method and enter the sender, connection details, and credential required by that method. Use a valid email address for the sender. 3. Fill Riciever Email Address as shown in the UI for the notification recipient and Email Header for the sender display header used in outgoing email. 4. Select Save. Leave the password or token field blank when you intend to retain the already saved value. Enter the replacement when rotating a credential. 5. Verify mail on an account and destination you control. For example, open the login screen and request Forgot Password for a test account, then check its inbox and spam folder. The Forgot Password action appears when the installation's configuration satisfies its mail readiness checks. Real delivery also depends on provider authorization, successful connection, and delivery to the recipient. If the link appears and no email arrives, verify the sender and credentials with the mail provider and check Console for the relevant timestamp. Keep credentials out of screenshots and support transcripts. See also Sign in and recover access, Manage user accounts, and Monitor server resources and alerts.

Change the general panel settings Open Settings → General to set the administration interface language and direction, editor defaults, CMS path, and email delivery. These settings apply at the installation level. Language and direction | Setting | What it controls | | --- | --- | | Panel language | The language used by panel controls that have translations. Use a short code such as en for English or fa for Persian. | | Data language | Default language context used by the panel when presenting data and editing controls. | | Panel direction | Layout direction for the panel. Enter ltr for left-to-right or rtl for right-to-left. | | Data direction | Reading and editing direction for data. Enter ltr or rtl as appropriate. | Enter the values and select Save. Reopen the relevant workspace to check the result. Manage the public website's language variants through Site languages. CMS Address CMS Address holds the segment between the site domain and /cms. For example, a value of panel produces an address such as https://example.com/panel/cms/. Enter a single URL-safe segment of up to 64 characters starting with a letter or number. The segment can also contain underscores and hyphens. Keep the site hostname, slashes, and protocol outside the field. Before modifying it, confirm the new address with anyone who links directly to the panel, save open work, and record both addresses for the transition. The new path can require an application restart to take effect. Use the site's login entry point to locate the panel again if an old bookmark fails, and check integration callback addresses that explicitly include the old path. editor CSS editor CSS is an optional CSS field used by the rich-text editor. Use it to make body text, headings, links, and other editor elements resemble their public rendering. Save, reopen a page with the rich-text editor, and verify a representative heading, paragraph, and list. Public layout and styling come from the active site theme. View the other Settings tabs Depending on your role, the workspace also includes Maintenance, OAuth, Search Console, and Analytics. The Analytics tab is the Google Analytics connection workspace. Integrations and operational actions have separate configuration. See also Email delivery, Maintenance, and Site General settings.

Restart the application or reset an installation Open Settings → Maintenance to find Server controls and Factory reset (day-1 state). These server actions require the built-in administrator. A restart briefly interrupts the application. A factory reset clears installation data and generated files. Restart application 1. Save open work and choose a suitable moment for the interruption. 2. Select Restart application under Server controls. 3. Read and confirm the Restart server prompt. 4. Wait for the hosting supervisor to start the application again. The panel attempts to reload after a short delay. If it reloads before the server is ready, refresh once it is back. 5. Sign in if needed and verify the panel, public site, and the action that led to the restart. Ask the hosting operator to check the service supervisor if the panel stays unavailable. The action exits the application process and relies on the supervisor to bring it back. Factory reset (day-1 state) Delete extras and reset to first install clears the MongoDB database and generated files, including themes or theme runtime files, uploads, public output, temporary files, and local backups. This is a full installation operation. 1. Confirm the intended site domain with the owner. Export or download the recovery files needed from the installation and keep them off the affected server. 2. In Factory reset (day-1 state), choose Delete extras and reset to first install. 3. Review the destructive-action confirmation. The panel asks you to type RESET exactly. 4. Wait for the result and the application reload. If the server returns a failure, record the message and have the operator inspect the actual data and runtime before making another attempt. 5. Follow the operator's recovery or first-install procedure, then verify site access and configuration. See also Configure backups, Download or restore a backup, and Set up a new BidoCMS installation.

Add, edit, activate, and deactivate user accounts Open Users → Users to manage accounts for the current installation. Use Search name or email to locate a record. The account table shows the role and whether the account is active or still needs a password change. Add a user 1. Make sure the intended role is available under Users → Roles. 2. In the Users tab, select Add user. 3. Enter First name, Last name, Display name, Email, and Phone number as applicable. Confirm the login email with the person. 4. Select a Role and keep Active account selected if access should begin immediately. 5. If the panel asks for a temporary password, set one with at least eight characters including a letter and a number and at most 72 UTF-8 bytes. Otherwise BidoCMS generates a temporary password and emails it to the new user. 6. Select Save. If a temporary password was set manually, share it privately with the user. They must create a different password on the first sign-in. With no configured email delivery, only a built-in administrator can create an account, using the manual temporary-password field. If Add user is unavailable and you manage user records, check this installation's mail configuration with your site administrator. Edit account details and role Select the user, review the fields in Edit user, make the change, and save. Editing an account record changes the user details, role, or active state. Password changes use the separate Reset password action for administrators or Profile → Security for the signed-in user. Activate or deactivate an account Use Activate or Deactivate and confirm the prompt. The account record is retained. Deactivation ends access, including from sessions that were already signed in. You cannot deactivate your own account, and the installation keeps at least one active built-in administrator. To grant access again, reactivate the existing account and verify its role. Reset its password separately if needed. Reset a user's password 1. Sign in as cms admin. 2. Open the user record and select Reset password. 3. Check the email or name shown in the Reset temporary password dialog. 4. If email is configured, select Email temporary password. To supply your own, choose Set a temporary password manually instead and select Set temporary password after filling the field. Installations without mail delivery show the manual option directly. 5. Confirm the success message and send the temporary password securely if you set it manually. Existing sessions end and the user must choose a fresh password at their next sign-in. See also Create roles and assign menu permissions, Sign in and recover access, and Configure email delivery.

Create roles and assign menu permissions Open Users → Roles to review role names and manage access to the sidebar menus and nested tabs. Users get the menu permissions of their assigned role. Create a role 1. Open Users and select Roles. 2. Check Search roles for a role that already fits the job. 3. Select New role and enter a clear Role name, such as Website editor. 4. Select the menu and submenu entries needed for the work. Selecting a parent selects its available descendants. Selecting a child selects its ancestors. Clearing a parent clears its descendants. 5. Review the resulting permissions and select Save. 6. Assign the role under Users → Users and verify it with an account that uses that role. A stored parent grant can exist without any child grants. For example, consider Settings, Settings → General, and Settings → Maintenance as separate entries. Open the parent in the permission tree, leave its needed child selected, and clear the child grants the role should not have. Scheduled or destructive actions within a workspace can also require built-in administrator access. Edit a role Select a role from the list, review its name and checkboxes, change the intended fields, and select Save. Roles created in this workspace can be renamed. Legacy and website-theme role names stay fixed so that site registration and ownership references keep working. Their editable menu grants remain available where the administrator is allowed to manage them. The system role cms admin always has full menu access. Its grants and name are fixed. A role editor can grant permissions only within their own permitted scope; the panel disables grants the current account cannot give. Understand what a grant applies to - Menu and submenu access are the units of permission for these roles. - A newly added submenu needs an explicit grant for a restricted role. - Account states still matter: a user with an appropriate role must also have an active account. - Website roles packaged with a theme may control public website behavior. Keep those roles separate from CMS administrator access when configuring the theme. - Some high-impact features apply additional checks. For example, deploying executable theme packages and operating SSH access require the built-in administrator. Troubleshoot missing access Ask the affected user for the exact menu and tab. Open their account record, confirm the assigned role, and then review both the parent and child grants under Roles. If the control still appears inaccessible after signing back in, check whether the installation has the feature configured and whether the feature requires cms admin. See also Manage user accounts and Find your way around the panel.

Download, restore, or delete a backup Backup → Backup Files lists the archives the installation has recorded, newest first. Restoring replaces installation data and typically restarts the application. Review and download a saved backup 1. Open Backup → Backup Files. 2. Match the record by Config, Description, and Time. 3. Review DB File and Data File. Each available archive shows its filename and size. 4. Select Download DB for the database archive or Download Files for the installation files archive. Keep both if a complete recovery requires both. 5. Verify the archive you intended to save before removing any older copy. A record can include just one archive, depending on its configuration. If the record exists but download fails, verify the configured destination and whether the archive is still present there. Restore from a saved record 1. Confirm the installation domain and record timestamp. Preserve a current copy of the affected data before replacing it. 2. In Backup Files, select Restore on the intended row. 3. Read the confirmation that current data will be overwritten, then confirm if the record is correct. 4. Wait for restore and restart. Reopen the panel, then verify the data and the public site. Check the recovery state if a restore that contained both parts fails midway. Restore from a local ZIP 1. Open Backup → Settings. 2. Set the restore selector to database for a database ZIP or file for a file backup ZIP. 3. Click Restore from File and select the matching BidoCMS archive. 4. Confirm Restore Backup. 5. Keep the page open until restoration or an error is reported. Archives larger than 32 MiB use chunked upload. Its progress can show an interrupted connection and retry. Cancel upload is available while the upload is running, before the server starts restoring. 6. Reconnect after the restart and test the restored installation. A database archive and a files archive are separate. When using the upload workflow, choose the matching type for each archive you need. Avoid launching another restore while one is still in progress. Delete a backup record and its archives Use the row's delete control and confirm Delete Backup. Verify the configuration, timestamp, and retained copies before confirming. The panel removes the record and requests removal of its archives from the configured destination. See also Configure backups and Restart the application or reset an installation.

Configure automatic and manual backups Backup → Settings lets you create separate configurations for database backups, file backups, or both. A configuration also controls the storage destination and automatic schedule. Backup actions require the built-in administrator. Create a configuration 1. Open Backup → Settings and select Add New Config. 2. Enter a Config Name you can recognize in backup history. 3. Choose Storage Format, then provide the destination details for that format. 4. Set Max Copies for retention and fill Destination Path where the chosen storage format uses it. 5. Enable Database Backup, Files Backup, or both. Review exclusions before continuing. 6. For automatic backups, enter a Cron Expression, such as 0 2 * * * for a run at 2 a.m. every day in the scheduler's time zone. Check the server time zone before scheduling for a specific local hour. 7. Select Create Config or Save Config. For scheduled backups, confirm Auto-backup: Active. Choose storage | Storage Format | Connection details | | --- | --- | | local | Uses the installation's backup storage. The configuration name determines its local backup grouping. | | s3 | Fill Region, Bucket, and Endpoint URL (optional) for the object store, plus the access and secret keys. A destination prefix can be used to group the files. | | ftp | Fill FTP Host / URL, the FTP username, and password. Verify endpoint reachability from the application server. | | sftp | Fill SFTP Host / URL (:port) and the username, then choose the SFTP Auth Method. Supply the password for password mode, or finish key authorization when using key mode. | Credential fields marked set only retain their existing stored values when left blank. In SFTP key mode, save first to generate the public-key installation command. Use Copy Command and ask the operator of the destination SFTP account to authorize that key on the target server. Generate new SSH key on save rotates the key. Authorize the replacement before relying on the next scheduled backup. Choose what to include Enable Database Backup creates a ZIP containing the MongoDB dump. Exclude Collections accepts comma-separated collection names. Leave it empty unless you deliberately intend to omit those collections. Enable Files Backup creates a separate ZIP of eligible installation file data. Exclude Routes accepts comma-separated path prefixes. Verify that excluding a path will leave the intended content restorable. Deployment secrets and protected runtime files are handled outside ordinary file backups. This screen has DB Archive Password (set only) and Files Archive Password (set only) fields. The current backup generation code writes ordinary ZIP archives. Protect the destination and downloads accordingly. Test and maintain the configuration 1. Save, then find Manual Backup in that configuration and select Run Backup Now. 2. Confirm the action and check Backup → Backup Files for the new record. 3. Verify the record includes the expected database and file archives. Download them or check their destination before relying on the automatic schedule. 4. Test restoring to an appropriate test installation. An invalid cron expression can leave automatic backup inactive. If a backup fails, check the destination configuration, provider permissions, and server Console. Retain needed archives independently before deleting a configuration. Its records and automatic schedule are removed from the panel. See also Download or restore a backup and Read the server console.

Read and download server console logs Open Console to see the application's captured server console. The built-in administrator can read, download, and clear the buffer. The workspace shows up to 500 recent lines with line numbers, refreshes every 15 seconds, and scrolls to the newest output after refresh. Read the logs 1. Note the time of the action you want to diagnose, such as a publication, backup, or connector operation. 2. Open Console and choose Refresh if you want the latest capture immediately. 3. Use Top and Bottom to move within the displayed lines. The status shows how many lines are displayed out of the total captured and when the view refreshed. 4. Select Download to export the full current in-memory log buffer as a text file. 5. Review and redact any sensitive values before sharing a log excerpt. Include the relevant time and preceding lines that establish which operation failed. Clear the captured buffer Clear asks for confirmation and clears the log buffer shared by the application. Download any evidence you need first. The buffer can start filling again as the server writes new messages. If the console is empty An empty view can appear when the buffer was cleared or the process has no captured logs. Refresh after reproducing the issue or check whether the server has been restarted to load the current capture support. Ask the hosting operator for deployment logs if you need process startup or historical data outside this buffer. See also Notifications dashboard and Monitor server resources and alerts.

Manage application environment variables Open Environment to inspect and change the installation's application variables as a built-in administrator. Changes apply to the application process and can affect service connectors, theme behavior, or runtime settings. Add or change a variable 1. Open Environment and allow the current rows to load. 2. For an existing variable, check its Name and update its Value. For a new variable, choose Add variable and complete both fields. 3. For multiple changes, verify each row is still present before saving. To remove a variable, choose the row's delete button and confirm Remove variable. 4. Choose Save variables. Use each name only once and fill the Name field in every row. Names must start with a letter or underscore and can contain letters, digits, and underscores. 5. Wait for the panel to reload. Verify the feature that uses the variable. Use Settings → Maintenance → Restart application if the feature reads its variables only at startup. Changes are encrypted in the installation database. The panel displays values to authorized operators, so keep them out of screenshots and support messages. Deployment-owned values remain in the hosting configuration. In Coolify deployments, persistent site data uses the dedicated /data volume. If a variable or restart is missing - If a deployment variable is absent from the list, check the hosting configuration with the server operator. - If an optional feature remains unavailable after saving, check its own requirements, then verify spelling and the selected installation. Restart the application if a startup-only value still needs to be loaded. - If the panel cannot load after saving, contact the server operator to review the service supervisor, runtime logs, and the changed value. See also Restart the application and Read the server console.

Export a BidoCMS website to WordPress Open Export to create a WordPress migration package for the current site. This feature is available to the built-in administrator and currently requires a single-site BidoCMS installation. It checks the installed theme and capabilities before building the package. Create and download a package 1. Open Export and verify the site address shown in the workspace. 2. Select WordPress under Destination CMS. 3. Choose Export website. Only one export can run for the site at a time. 4. Watch Export history for the new record. The panel updates pending exports while you are in the workspace. You can use Refresh or reopen the workspace to reload the persisted history. 5. Select Download ZIP when the export shows Ready. Use Details to review errors or compatibility notes when they are available. | Status | Meaning | | --- | --- | | Queued | The request is recorded and waiting to run. | | Preparing | The export is checking compatibility or building the package. | | Ready | The package is available for download. | | Failed | Open compatibility notes or details and review the unsupported behavior or reported failure. | Use Delete and confirm Delete export to remove a ready or failed record and its saved package. Keep any ZIP you still need. Read the package contents The ZIP includes a generated WordPress theme and the BidoCMS Importer plugin, the migrated content payload, local public assets, a content-only WXR file, the export manifest, and restoration instructions. Use the bundled RESTORE.md for the package-specific workflow. Keep extracted source content and other migration material outside the web root unless the instructions identify a supported destination. Compatible layouts continue to use editable content bindings on WordPress. Server-side routes, application models, custom scripts, and provider integrations can require dedicated WordPress implementations. Detected unsupported capabilities can block export. Review compatibility details before treating the package as a replacement for the site. Restore and verify on WordPress 1. Prepare a single-site WordPress installation using the version and PHP requirements in RESTORE.md. Start on staging so you can verify the result before moving public traffic. 2. Extract the downloaded ZIP outside the destination web root. Copy the supplied wp-content contents to the WordPress installation as directed by the included instructions. 3. Activate BidoCMS Importer and open Tools → BidoCMS Restore. Start the restore using a WordPress administrator account. 4. Under Settings → Website theme, review each Language website address. Save Settings → Permalinks to refresh rewrite rules. 5. Verify important page routes, language versions, images, published content, redirects, metadata, forms, and integrations. Keep the importer active because it provides the imported routing and redirects. The ZIP contains content.xml for a separate content-only workflow. Use either WXR import or the bundled full restoration on the destination, according to the outcome you want. See also Configure backups and Site languages.

Browse and manage installation files Open Files to work with accessible files in the installation storage. This workspace is for administrators. Images is the separate workspace for the site's managed media records and image metadata. Browse and select - Use the folder breadcrumbs and Up to move around the allowed storage root. Select Refresh to reload the current folder. - On desktop, double-click a folder or file to open it. On touch screens, tap the entry's name. With a keyboard, focus the name and activate it. - Use the row checkboxes or the header checkbox to select items for toolbar actions. Name, Size, and Modified help identify the current copy. - Supported images open a preview, and supported text files open an editor. Toolbar actions | Action | How to use it | | --- | --- | | New folder | Open the parent folder, choose New folder, and enter the folder name. | | Upload | Open the destination, select Upload, and choose one or more files. Check the refreshed list after the upload confirms. | | Download | Select files and choose Download. For a directory, create a ZIP first and download the ZIP. | | Edit | Select exactly one supported text file and choose Edit. Make the change and select Save or Cancel. | | Rename | Select exactly one item, choose Rename, and enter its new name. | | Copy, Cut, and Paste | Select the source items, choose Copy to duplicate or Cut to move, navigate to the target folder, and select Paste. | | Zip | Select the files or folders, choose Zip, and enter an archive name. The archive is created in the current folder. | | Unzip | Select one .zip file and choose Unzip. Extraction targets the current folder. Review the results in that folder. | | Delete | Select the intended items, choose Delete, verify the number in the confirmation, and confirm removal. | If a file cannot be changed The editor can read supported text files up to 1 MiB and accepts saves up to 2 MiB. For larger files or unsupported extensions, use your approved external workflow. Operations also enforce path, file, and archive checks. Protected data, security-sensitive paths, and invalid archives may be rejected. If a move or extraction fails, start by checking the destination, available space, and the error message. Avoid editing generated output when the long-term change belongs in the source page or theme, since publishing can replace generated output. See also Publish site changes and SSH access.

Monitor server resources and configure alerts Open Monitor to check resource use for the BidoCMS process and its runtime, view history, and create email alerts for sustained resource conditions. The monitor API requires the built-in administrator. Read the live cards Live values refresh about every 10 seconds. The Runtime line identifies the environment and the time of the last update. | Card | App consumption | Available to app | | --- | --- | --- | | CPU | CPU usage reported for the CMS process. | CPU capacity in the application runtime's scope. | | RAM | Process resident memory, shown as RSS. | Available memory in the runtime pool. | | Disk | Size of the CMS project on disk. | Free space on the disk or volume used by the application. | Open How to verify these numbers to compare the raw readings with the operating system. A container can have a different resource limit from the full host. If Available to app stays blank after an update, follow the monitor's restart message or ask the server operator to check that the current monitor service is running. Use the history chart Choose a Time range from one hour, six hours, one day, seven days, 30 days, or one year. The one-hour through one-day ranges use one-minute buckets, seven days uses hourly buckets, and the longer windows use daily buckets. The chart refreshes about once a minute. - Toggle cpu average, ram average, disk, database size, and the inbound or outbound network series as needed. - cpu candle and ram candle show the minimum and maximum in each time bucket with a tick for the average. Average lines show one average per bucket. - Move over the chart to inspect a measurement with its timestamp. Check the unit and the selected series. Database size and network totals are byte measurements, while resource percentage series use percentages. - Gaps represent missing readings. The chart can mark recorded process restarts, server restarts, and factory resets. Add and maintain alert rules 1. Under Alert rules, select Add rule. 2. Enter a descriptive Rule name of at most 50 characters. 3. Choose a Metric. CPU and RAM each have process and host/container options. Disk metrics cover the project and its volume. Database size and inbound/outbound network totals are also available. 4. Set a positive Threshold (numeric) and a positive Duration in minutes (numeric). Use a threshold meaningful for the chosen metric's unit. The alert condition depends on the metric staying at or above the threshold for the specified duration. 5. Enter one recipient per line in Emails (one address per line) and save. Both the row Save and Save alert settings submit the current rule list, so complete any other draft rows before saving. 6. To remove a rule, choose the row's Delete. Check the resulting list for the remaining rules. Check Settings → General for email readiness if alerts do not arrive. Verify the metric, threshold, duration, and recipients before assuming an alert missed an event. See also Dashboard system health, Read the server console, and Configure email delivery.

Open the Notes workspace Notes is a sidebar menu entry that opens an empty workspace in the current shared BidoCMS panel. It displays There is nothing to display yet. The current view provides no controls for creating, editing, saving, or sharing notes. Locate the menu Open the sidebar or the mobile navigation drawer and select Notes. Ask your administrator to review the role grant if you expected to see the entry. Site-specific tools can have their own documentation and controls when supplied by the installation's theme or app. See also Find your way around the BidoCMS panel.

Configure and run installed theme scripts Open Scripts to view background scripts supplied by the installed theme or installation. Script operations require the built-in administrator. Each script can have a different set of named inputs. Configure one script 1. Find the script by script name. Use file name to confirm the installed script you intend to change. 2. Enter script time (seconds) to set its interval for group launches. A positive value repeats the script at that interval. A value of zero runs it once. 3. Fill the inputs defined by that script. The input names and acceptable values depend on its implementation. 4. Select Save for that script and check the success or error message. 5. Select start on its row and confirm Start script to run that script once. Start or stop all scripts Start All Scripts starts active installed scripts as a group using their configured intervals. Stop All Scripts stops them as a group. Both actions ask for confirmation. Check which scripts are installed before using a group action. A script can change public data or communicate with an external service. Troubleshoot If the expected script is missing, verify the installed theme or script package with its maintainer. If starting a script returns an error, note the script name, the action, and the exact time, then check Console for its output. Review provider or script input requirements before trying the action again. See also Read the server console.

Register an SSH key and connect to the site Open SSH access to register public keys, read the site's connection information, and follow connection instructions. Site administrators manage up to three named public keys for the installation. Register a key 1. In Connection guide, open Create a key on your computer and follow the instructions for macOS, Windows 10 or 11, or Linux. 2. Copy one complete line from the public key file ending in .pub. Use Ed25519 or RSA with at least 3072 bits. 3. Select Add public key, enter a Key name from 1 to 80 characters, and paste the line into Public key (.pub). 4. Save and review the key's fingerprint and Added date. Keep the private key and its passphrase on your own device. 5. Use Rename to change the identifying label. Use Delete and confirm to revoke that key when a device is retired or access should end. Use the connection details Connection details lists the SSH hostname, port, username, and server fingerprint with the database details where configured. | Connection guide | Use it to | | --- | --- | | Connect with MongoDB Compass | Configure the site's database details and SSH tunnel in the Compass interface. Reference for built-in BidoCMS MCP tools Open MCP Server → BidoCMS Tools to choose which built-in read tools an MCP client can use. The installed MCP documentation shows the current installation's exposed tools. Tool names are the identifiers clients call. | Tool | Purpose | Inputs | | --- | --- | --- | | site-info | Read general site information, supported languages and page types. | None. | | list-node-types | List the site's page types and page counts. | None. | | list-nodes | List pages by optional type, language, publication state or text. | typeName, language, publishedOnly, search, limit, skip. | | get-node | Get a page's localized metadata, specifications and text. | Supply a url, nodeId or internal shenase to identify the page. | | list-specifications | Read specification definitions, optionally limited to a page type. | Optional typeName. | | search-content | Search text and page metadata and return matching pages and URLs. | Required query, optional limit. | Choose scope and verify access 1. Enable the tools needed for the client, decide which require a token and choose Save BidoCMS Tools. 2. For a protected tool, open Access Tokens and grant that tool explicitly. 3. From the client, call site-info or list-node-types first when the relevant language or page type is uncertain. 4. To browse a larger result set with list-nodes, use limit and skip. The default limit is 50 and the maximum is 500. Set publishedOnly when the query should be limited to published pages. The tool's default for this filter is false. 5. search-content defaults to 20 results and accepts up to 100. If the results include several language versions, use the returned URL to identify the intended page before retrieving more detail. A read-only operation can still expose content. Review the result scope before marking a built-in tool public. An enabled tool requiring a token remains unavailable without a valid grant. Configure tool definitions · Grant an access token

Configure MCP Server and connect an AI client Open MCP Server → Settings to enable the installation's Model Context Protocol endpoint. MCP provides configured tools to external AI clients using Streamable HTTP. Enable and find the endpoint 1. Open MCP Server → Settings. 2. Turn on Enable MCP Server. The setting saves when the checkbox changes. 3. Select Copy Endpoint URL. The installation's endpoint usually ends in /mcp. 4. Select Open MCP Documentation to open the installation's MCP reference in a new tab. 5. Add the endpoint to a compatible client as a Streamable HTTP server. For a protected tool, configure the Bearer token provided by a CMS administrator. 6. Check the client's available tools. The tool must be enabled and, for protected calls, granted to the token. Understand access by tool | Policy | What the client needs | | --- | --- | | Public | The endpoint URL. No token or grant is required for callers. | | Requires access token | The client sends Authorization: Bearer <token>, and that token needs an explicit grant for the tool. | | OAuth only | The policy can be stored, but MCP OAuth is pending. The tool is unavailable. | | Disabled | The tool is unavailable to the client. | Use BidoCMS Tools for built-in read-only tools, Panel Tools for panel-authored tools, API Tools for API-authored tools and Theme Tools for definitions supplied by a theme. Access Tokens manages grants. A discovery warning after enabling indicates that the MCP setting saved but public discovery output did not sync. Check publish storage and use Rebuild Sitemap if instructed by the panel. If a single tool is missing, check its enabled state and token policy before changing endpoint configuration. Create and manage MCP access tokens Open MCP Server → Access Tokens to grant an external MCP client access to specific enabled Bearer-protected tools. Create and copy a token 1. Ensure that the target tool is enabled and marked Requires access token. 2. Open Access Tokens → New Token. 3. Enter a Name that identifies the consuming client or automation. 4. Set Expiry Date (optional). Leaving it blank gives the token no automatic expiration. 5. Under Tool Access, check the individual tools the client needs. Only enabled Bearer-protected tools appear in this list. Public tools need no selection. 6. Choose Create Token, then Copy Token from the one-time reveal. 7. Store the token in the intended client's credential settings, supplied as Authorization: Bearer <token>. Choose Done — Hide Token in the panel when finished. Review, edit or remove access The token list shows the token name, masked value, expiry, tool access and last used information. Edit changes the name, expiry or explicit tool grants. New tools need to be granted separately. Use the enabled control to suspend a token where available or Delete to remove it. If you lose the secret value, create a replacement token for the client, then remove the old token. If an otherwise valid token cannot call a tool, verify the token is enabled and unexpired, check the specific grant, and confirm the tool's current access mode. If no selectable tools appear while creating a token, configure an enabled tool with Bearer protection first. Connect an AI client · Set a tool access policy

Inspect a page's Google indexing status Open Pages → selected page → selected language → Search Engines to read Google's stored URL Inspection result for that language's public URL. You need access to the page and Pages → Search Engines, along with an active Search Console connection. Check the URL and Google observation 1. Verify the displayed public URL and language. 2. Check the headline status and any coverage detail. The panel can display URL is indexed, URL is not indexed or Index status is unknown, as reported by Google. 3. Read Last checked for the time the CMS retrieved the observation and Last Google crawl for the time Google's crawler last fetched that URL. The timestamps can differ. 4. Choose Check now if the first scheduled inspection is pending, or Check again to request a fresh observation. Checks for the same URL have a five-minute minimum interval and use Google quota. If refreshing is temporarily unavailable, check the availability time on the refresh control. 5. Choose Open in Search Console when you need the Google interface itself. The CMS retrieves Google's recorded state and does not submit a live URL test or indexing request. Interpret the sections | Section | What you can learn | | --- | --- | | Crawling and indexing | When Google crawled, crawler type, robots.txt result, page fetch result and indexing directives. | | Canonical URLs | The canonical the page declared and the canonical Google selected. Compare both with the intended public URL. | | Known sitemaps | Sitemaps Google supplied for the inspected URL. | | Referring pages | Example URLs Google reported as referring pages for this URL. This list is not a complete backlink inventory. | | Rich results | Structured data types and issues returned by Google, when available. Expand or read individual issue information before changing the page schema. | | AMP version | Optional AMP observations when Google reports them. | | Mobile usability · legacy report | Optional legacy field returned by Google. | | Report information | Property and observation timing. | | Inspection history | Previous observations retained for the URL, with coverage and crawl details for comparison. | Not reported indicates a missing field in the inspection response. Newly published content and translations can await their first scheduled check. Opening a pending URL displays the available observation state while the collector continues in the background. Diagnose an unexpected result If Google reports a robots.txt block, a noindex directive, a fetch failure or an unexpected canonical, compare the observation with the actual public page and its current publishing settings. A recent publishing change can be newer than the last crawl. An empty Performance report describes traffic availability and is a separate signal from indexing status.
